jobs.occupation: Associate Professor Clinical Pharmacy
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a full time permanent position as Associate Professor in Clincal Pharmacy at the Section for Pharmaceutics and Social Pharmacy, Department of Pharmacy, University of Oslo.
About the Department and what we are looking for in this position
The Department of Pharmacy at the University of Oslo is seeking a highly motivated, dynamic, and innovative researcher with strong collaborative and educational skills. The Department has a strong interdisciplinary environment that covers the key areas of the pharmaceutical field. Cutting-edge research, extensive national and international collaboration, and an integrated Master’s programme in Pharmacy position the Department as a key contributor to the development of pharmacy in Norway. We place strong emphasis on collaboration with the healthcare sector, regulatory authorities, as well as the pharmaceutical industry. The Section for Pharmaceutics and Social pharmacy is one of the three sections at the Department of Pharmacy and is comprised of strong research groups specializing in clinical pharmacy, as well as pharmacoepidemiology and pharmaceutics. The section offers an active and dynamic academic environment, ideal for ambitious researchers. The research environment (Clinical pharmacy - Department of Pharmacy) focuses on patient safety, medication use, and continuity of care, supported by methodological expertise spanning from qualitative studies to randomised trials, as well as health care innovation and strong collaboration with healthcare partners in the Oslo region.
 
The life science environment in the Oslo region is developing steadily, supported by collaboration between the pharmaceutical sector, the university hospital and hospital pharmacy, and academic institutions. Oslo Science City and the new Life Science Building are central initiatives contributing to this development. The Department of Pharmacy is relocating to the new Life Science Building in 2026 (Life Science building- UiO:Livsvitenskap). This move will provide modern facilities designed to strengthen research, teaching, and collaboration across the health and life science disciplines at the University of Oslo. 

The ideal candidate will play an important role in shaping the department’s activities in the new Life Science Building by contributing to the development of pharmaceutical sciences within a strong interdisciplinary environment. In particular, the candidate is expected to strengthen research and academic activity to contribute to the research group’s collaboration with healthcare partners and other research groups. Documented experience with interdisciplinary work and international cooperation is highly desirable.

The successful candidate should have documented independent research experience in addition to the PhD degree with publications in international peer review journals. Furthermore, the candidate should have a documented history of securing significant external funding, or at least strong funding application efforts.  
Your main tasks will be
• Teaching and supervision, mainly in social pharmacy, at all levels of the five-years study program in pharmacy, including master- and PhD. 
• Course leadership for the main course in social pharmacy at the undergraduate program.
• Initiating and conducting high quality research within the research group’s focus areas, including contributing to external funding.
• Contributing to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Carrying out examination related duties and contributing to academic administration as required. More information about the position
Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field, equivalent to an Associate professor position. The successful applicant must be able to teach at all levels and to supervise Master and PhD students. The successful applicant may furthermore be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks, by request from the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. 
What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications that must be documented in the application::

• The successful applicant must have completed a PhD preferably in clinical or social pharmacy and have a strong scientific track record within the area.
• Master’s degree in pharmacy or equivalent must be formally documented. 
• Scientific qualifications will play a major role, with main emphasis placed on research output from the last five years. 
• Documented potential for further acquisition of external funding.
• Documented knowledge of Scandinavian pharmaceutical practice and traditions.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe her/his qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time
• A researching approach
• A collegial attitude and practice
• The successful candidate who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
• Teaching in the pharmacy program is conducted primarily in Norwegian. Applicants are required to document proficiency in Norwegian at a minimum level of B2. The successful candidate must also demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills in Norwegian, or another Scandinavian language, in relevant assessment settings such as a trial lecture and interview.
Desired qualifications:

• Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. A track record in scientific and administrative management is an advantage.
• An international research network and documented experience with international collaboration.
• Ability to contribute to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Experience with working within the European healthcare setting, for example pharmacy, or with interprofessional collaboration
• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience with independent teaching responsibilities and with the development of study programmes.
• Experience with planning and conducting of clinical trials as well as regulatory experience in drug development. What are we looking for in you?
• Strong communication skills with students and colleagues.
• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive, supporting and productive research environment
• Strong networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate is expected to have an international profile in relation to the criteria outlined above. Selection for this position will be based on academic excellence and the candidate’s fit within the research group and the group’s research profile. In addition, pedagogical competence and personal suitability for contributing to a collaborative and supportive academic environment will form part of the overall assessment.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Modern facilities in the new Life Science Building.
• Opportunities for academic leadership and career development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Associate Professor (position code 1011) in salary range NOK from 750 000 - to 950 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, two % is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund. We need different perspectives in our work
University of Oslo is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

Men are encouraged to apply. The field of clinical pharmacy currently has an uneven gender balance, with women overrepresented among permanent academic staff, and the department wishes to contribute to a better gender balance within the field.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
How to apply
The application must include:

• Application letter
• A research position paper (1–4 pages) describing the applicant’s vision and scientific ambitions for the near future, as well as strategies for collaboration and for identifying synergies with the existing group.
• A detailed CV, including a complete list of education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative management, project acquisition and coordination experience, and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of educational certificates, PhD diploma, transcript of records and letters of recommendation
• A complete list of publications and academic merits and awards (if not included in the CV)
• Full text of up to 10 selected scientific publications the applicant wishes to include in the evaluation
• A document discussing the importance, interrelation, and relevance of the selected papers for this position
• Educational portfolio of 3–6 pages documenting educational competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own teaching practice and view of learning is anchored in the SoTL framework (focus on student learning, development over time, a researching approach and a collegial attitude and practice) 
• List of reference persons: 2–3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
As a general rule an interview will be used in the appointment process, usually supplemented with a trial teaching session. The basis for assessment will be the scientific production of the applicant, the teaching portfolio, pedagogical and educational qualifications, the applicant’s qualifications within leadership and administration, other qualifications as well as general personal suitability for the position. In ranking the competent applicants, the full range of qualifications will be considered and explicitly assessed.

Rules for appointments to associate professorships. https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-appointment-professor.htmlRules for the assessment and weighting of pedagogical competence for appointments to permanent academic posts which include teaching duties: https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-basic-pedagogical-competence.html
 
Guide for applicants for Professor and Associate professor positions - University of Oslo https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/guide-applicants.html

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova), information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results, see: http://www.uio.no/english/for-employees/employment/work-results/

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The Department of Pharmacy has 130 employees. We have an active research and innovation environment based on independent research in pharmaceutical topics. The Department of Pharmacy is responsible for the popular master's degree program in pharmacy and has 350 competent and committed students.
Pharmaceutical related research and education forms the base of all activities at the Department of Pharmacy. The science of pharmacy lies in the interface between the natural sciences, pharmaceutical technology, health related topics and social sciences. This interdisciplinarity is reflected both in our study programmes and in our research. 
In the planned life science building at the University of Oslo, closer collaboration with health enterprises, local government and the business sector will enhance quality and relevance in research and education of the future labour force. The building will be the heart of the first innovation district in Norway – Oslo Science City. The Department of Pharmacy will move into the new Life Science building in 2026.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate Distributed Value-stacking Flexibility for Efficient Distribution Grid Operation
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electrical power engineering, operations research, or a related field, and are you interested in energy systems and markets? As a PhD candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, both in and outside academia. 

The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years as part of the NTNU Energy initiative on Resilient and Integrated Energy Systems. You will join the research group Electricity Markets and Energy System Planning (EMESP) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Our work environment is defined by its friendly and supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to end the week. These formal and informal events offer opportunities to share ideas, celebrate milestones, and build relationships. PhD candidates also organize social activities open to everyone interested, fostering a welcoming and inclusive community.

Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department.
About the project
Globally, electricity demand is increasing and expected to increase in the coming years, supported by higher consumption from industrial actors, increasing electrification and integration of electric vehicles, data centers and other electrical sources. The electrical grid is getting increasingly strained due to the increased load, which needs to handle the power-intense appliances, while also needing to enable more renewable energy production into the power system. In both the EU and Norway, the ageing distribution grid is expected to have challenges in the future year due to the energy transition, needing investments and reinforcements to prevent critical situations such as voltage issues and bottlenecks in the grid. To combat these issues due to long lead time on investments and immature replacement situations, flexibility is seen as a vital part to enable more active operation of the electrical grid to prolong secure operational conditions. Ensuring local flexible resources in local distributional grids can be enabled for grid support and be integrated as part of the operational solutions without impacting their own operational situations to a large degree will be key to understanding and assessing the potential available. 

The objective of this PhD project is to develop new knowledge, models, methods, and analytical insights into how flexible resources can be utilized to provide grid support to the local distribution grid, while also participating in defined electrical markets and balancing markets. The flexible resources aim to maximize their revenues through different market options, and the consequences this will have on the local distribution grid. How upholding local conditions can be performed will be important to enable value-stacking grid services in an efficient manner. Local distributional systems operators (DSOs) might not have defined specific local markets for grid support, and how this service impacts other revenue streams and how TSO-DSO-coordination impacts operations will need to be analyzed. The project will focus on how these local conditions can be accounted for in long-term operational planning by the flexible provider, while also being accounted for during short-term operational decisions and reserve market activation sequences. Use of both active and reactive power to enable efficient grid operations will be a key aspect to approach this work.

The PhD candidate will develop and apply optimization-based models that capture the dynamics of the electricity grid and different flexible providers in the distributional grid (for instance, but not limited to batteries, EV parking lots, industrial demand, etc.). Key focus will be put into methods that can simplify grid information, to reduce the need for grid-sensitive information during operational planning and operation. Regulatory aspects and TSO-DSO coordination schemes will also need to be addressed and investigated as part of the project. 

The PhD candidate will be hosted by the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group in the Department of Electric Energy at NTNU. The main supervisor will be Associate Professor Kasper Emil Thorvaldsen, with co-supervision from relevant experts in power system operation and optimization, depending on the final methodological focus of the PhD project.
Duties of the position
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above
• Participate in activities of the EMESP research group 
• Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum 30 ECTS
• Contribute to publications in relevant journals and to popular science dissemination
• 
Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions

Career-enhancing work, which is in addition to the research project and doctoral education, may be offered to a candidate who demonstrates clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department determines there is a need. Examples of career-enhancing work include, but are not limited to, contributing to teaching, laboratory and exercise teaching, supervision, and examination work within the employee's areas of competence. 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in either electrical power engineering, control engineering, managerial economics with strong quantitative skills, or physics or mathematics with a specialization in operations research. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master's students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than August 2027.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, i.e., by having relevant work experience and/or published/publishable scientific papers in the field of the proposed research area.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Faculty's Doctoral Programme.
• You must have English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Applicants who are not native English speakers are encouraged to document their English language proficiency. This can be done through an approved English language test. One of the following test scores could be documented for this purpose: 
• TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 79 - 101. 
• IELTS - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 5.5 - 6.0 
• Cambridge English - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 160 - 179.
• Further assessment of both written and oral English language skills, as well as the ability to communicate fluently, will be conducted throughout the selection process and during any interviews for all applicants.Preferred selection criteria
• Master’s thesis or relevant work experience relevant to the announced position.
• Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, Julia or R- programming language.
• Experience with optimization modelling and electricity markets and power flow.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), the candidate is expected to: 

• demonstrate strong motivation, curiosity, and a learning-oriented mindset
• work independently, take initiative, and maintain good structure and discipline in their work
• communicate effectively and collaborate well with supervisors and peers
• show resilience and work constructively when facing challenges or setbacks
• demonstrate integrity and a strong sense of responsibility in their research conduct
Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Social activities organized by PhD Students
• Weekly social gathering on Fridays (Friday coffee)
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)  
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
• As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years, with the possibility of an additional 3 to 12 months of employment related to career-enhancing activities. 

The option for career-enhancing work may be offered to a candidate who has clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department deems it necessary. This will be clarified with the candidate during and after any interview. 

If you cannot document skills in Norwegian, Swedish, or Danish at level A2 upon employment, NTNU offers the opportunity to take Norwegian courses corresponding to at least 15 credits. NTNU will facilitate this. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Electric Power Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• A cover letter where the applicant explains personal motivation, briefly summarizes scientific work, and describes how their background is a good fit (400 words/1 page).
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project, and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages, including references). This proposal shall neither be deemed final nor binding for the project.
• CV.
• If you have testimonials of work experience, submit them.
• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees. If you have not yet completed your Master's thesis, you must provide confirmation of your estimated submission date for the Master's thesis, or confirmation that your Master's thesis has been submitted.
• Applicants from universities outside Norway are asked to provide a diploma supplement or similar document that details the study program and grading system. Also, see the specific documentation requirements for education obtained outside Norway, applicable to certain regions or countries, here.  
• A copy of the Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you are encouraged to include a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be provided before assuming the position. 
• If you have publications or other relevant research work, submit them.
• You are encouraged to include documentation of English language proficiency if you are not a native speaker of English. 
• Name and contact information of three referees.
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. 

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellow in Recognizing Content Generated with AI
jobs.employer_name: NTNU FAKULTET FOR INFORMASJONS- TEKNOLOGI OG ELEKTRONIKK
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,600 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

     
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
As AI systems become increasingly available, we encounter more and more content that has been generated. Examples include text, images, audio, videos, as well as software. In some instances, it is crucial to be able to identify content that had been generated. Financial institutions need a solid basis to assess loan applications. Universities need to assure that submitted essays are the work of the student. Recruiters need to be able to tell whether an application is authentic.

The position aims to develop methods to help identify generated content. Initially, the candidate will need to get a firm grip of the state of the art already available to identify AI-generated content. Later, the candidate conducts experiments with different models and methodologies to indicate the presence or absence of generated content. We plan to publish the results in peer reviewed conferences or journals.

Your immediate leader will be the head of the DART unit.

Are you ready to take your research career to the next level? We offer an exciting 3-year postdoctoral position that gives you the opportunity to develop a strong profile as researcher. You will also gain valuable experience that might be relevant for your further career.The purpose of a postdoctoral position is to build up a researcher profile that qualifies for a position as associate professor. The position may also offer additional skills that are relevant to the postdoctoral fellow's future career.

Apply for this position to become part of our research environment and take the next step in your career with us.
About the project 
The position is associated with the AURA project. The project aims to advance the understanding in, and the development of AI to improve the region. The position is part of the work package on AI and safety. AI-generated can be used to mislead organizations. For instance, banks need to verify documents in the process of approving loans, companies need to verify the authenticity of applications, and municipalities need to authenticate communication with citizens.
Duties of the position
• Carry out high-quality research within the area of the position.
• Deploy your work in collaboration with industrial partners of the region (if relevant).
• Produce academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the work associated with the AURA project .
• Mentoring MSc students, helping them with their research projects, and advising on methodology and academic writing.
• Unless proficient in a Scandinavian language, the candidate will attend Norwegian courses.Required selection criteria
• You must have completed a doctoral degree in Machine Learning, Statistics, or similar. 
• You must have a professionally relevant background in algorithms, machine learning, database systems, or data mining.
• Experience with different generative AI approaches such as transformer, or diffusion models.
• Very good programming skills in either Python, Julia, or R.
• Have excellent skills in mathematics and probabilistic AI.
• Good written and oral English

In such cases, you will also be assigned relevant teaching as part of the career-promoting work.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions and for general criteria for the position.

• Experience with implementing prototypic systems to demonstrate research results (provide link to GitHub/GitLab or similar)

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electrical power engineering, operations research, or a related field, and are you interested in energy systems and markets? As a PhD candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, both in and outside academia. 

The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years. You will join the research group Electricity Markets and Energy System Planning (EMESP) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Our work environment is defined by its friendly and supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to end the week. PhD candidates also organize social activities open to everyone interested, fostering a welcoming and inclusive community.

Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The doctoral candidate is expected to investigate and develop optimization-based mathematical models for reserve procurement and balancing energy in liberalized electricity systems. Particular attention will be given to: i) the construction of market bids based on fundamental market models, in which the representation of non-convex cost components is important, and ii) the timing of reserve procurement, investigating the potential benefits of co-optimizing reserve procurement and wholesale energy. This research will involve mathematical programming, including modeling of the hydropower system and stochastic optimization methods. The models developed will be used to analyze how different market designs affect the costs and prices of procuring reserve capacity and delivering balancing energy. The work will also aim to provide insights that are relevant for the further development of efficient and well-functioning balancing markets. 

The PhD candidate will be hosted in the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group at the Department of Electric Energy, NTNU. The main supervisor will be Professor Arild Helseth, with co-supervision from experts in balancing markets and market design, including Professor Hossein Farahmand (NTNU) and Research Manager Stefan Jaehnert (SINTEF Energy). The Norwegian TSO Statnett will serve as a discussion partner in this project.

jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced and hands-on Head of Warehouse to lead and develop our warehouse and material-flow operations in a growing production environment.

The role combines people leadership, operational management, inventory control, material planning, production support, and continuous improvement. You will be responsible for ensuring that materials and components are available at the right time and in the right quantity, while maintaining high standards of inventory accuracy, efficiency, quality, safety, and production support.

You will work closely with Production, Purchasing, Planning, Quality, Logistics, and Management to ensure a reliable and efficient flow of materials throughout the organization.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you will be expected to both lead the warehouse team and stay close to daily operations.

In this role you will be responsible for:
Warehouse Operations & Material Flow
• 
Lead and coordinate daily warehouse operations, including receiving, inspection, storage, picking, kitting, internal material supply, packing, and outbound shipments.

• 
Ensure efficient and reliable material flow between warehouse, production, testing, and other operational areas.

• 
Ensure materials and components are correctly identified, stored, handled, and supplied to production.

• 
Coordinate loading and unloading activities in accordance with safety requirements.

• 
Ensure finished products, materials, and equipment are correctly prepared and documented for shipment.

• 
Develop and maintain an organized, efficient, and scalable warehouse structure.
Inventory Management
• 
Take overall responsibility for inventory accuracy and stock control.

• 
Establish and maintain routines for cycle counting, stock checks, reconciliation, and investigation of discrepancies.

• 
Monitor stock levels and proactively identify potential shortages or supply risks.

• 
Follow up on damaged, obsolete, or slow-moving inventory.

• 
Ensure all warehouse transactions and material movements are correctly registered in the ERP/WMS system.

• 
Develop and improve inventory-control processes as the company grows.
Production Planning & Material Supply
• 
Work closely with Production and Planning to ensure materials and components are available according to production requirements.

• 
Support production planning through accurate information on stock levels, material availability, and lead times.

• 
Develop and maintain efficient parts-kitting processes, ensuring production orders receive the correct components and quantities.

• 
Establish and improve material replenishment processes, including Kanban and pull-based systems where appropriate.

• 
Identify and resolve material-flow issues that may affect production.
ERP, Systems & Reporting
• 
Take ownership of warehouse-related processes and data in the ERP/WMS system.

• 
Ensure accurate receiving, issuing, transfers, picking, stock control, packing, shipping, and documentation.

• 
Use warehouse and inventory data to monitor performance and support operational decision-making.

• 
Establish relevant warehouse KPIs and follow up on performance.

• 
Support the implementation and development of warehouse systems, tools, and processes.
You have:
• 
Several years of progressive experience in warehouse management, inventory control, materials management, logistics, or a related field.

• 
Previous experience in a warehouse leadership or supervisory role.

• 
Experience from a manufacturing, industrial, engineering, or technically complex production environment is highly desirable.

• 
Strong practical experience with receiving, storage, picking, kitting, inventory management, material handling, and shipping.

• 
Experience supporting production planning and material requirements.

• 
Strong understanding of inventory control, stock accuracy, cycle counting, reconciliation, and replenishment.

• 
Practical experience with Kanban, pull systems, lean material flow, or similar replenishment processes is an advantage.

• 
Strong experience with ERP/WMS systems and warehouse data.

• 
Experience using data and KPIs to monitor and improve warehouse performance.

• 
Experience developing warehouse procedures, routines, and work instructions.

• 
Experience with 5S, continuous improvement, or lean principles is an advantage.

• 
Good forklift experience; T1, T2, and T4 certification is an advantage.

• 
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• 
Ability to prioritize and make decisions in a fast-paced production environment.

• 
English — fluent or strong professional working level.

• 
Ukrainian/Norwegian — an advantage.
What We Offer
• 
An opportunity to join a growing technology company at an exciting stage of development

• 
Meaningful responsibility and direct impact on products and processes

• 
A collaborative and international working environment

• 
Professional development and career growth opportunities

• 
Competitive compensation and benefits package

We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

About the project
Power system state estimation is a key function in transmission system operation, as many higher-level monitoring, security assessment, and control applications rely on reliable estimates of the system state. State estimators combine measurements with mathematical grid models and must remain robust to erroneous data and missing measurements.

Building on these challenges, the PhD candidate will contribute to research activities within the p-SWAMP project. The research focuses on the development and evaluation of linear state estimation methods under realistic operating conditions, including challenges related to power system observability. Furthermore, the research investigates how uncertainties in state estimation affect the reliability of voltage stability indicators.

The main supervisor for the PhD is Associate Professor Daniel Baltensperger, and the co-supervisor will be Professor Kjetil Obstfelder Uhlen.

• Publish scientific results and contribute to research dissemination.

Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum of 30 ECTS.

jobs.occupation: Researcher position in computational chemistry
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a Researcher position in computational chemistry, available at the Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry.

The position is for a period of 2 years.

Starting date no later than 01.03.2027.

Place of work is Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry at Blindern, Oslo.
Project description
The position is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists (FRIPRO) “APExModel: Addressing Antimicrobial Peptides by Integrating Experiments into Modelling” and lead by Henrique Musseli Cezar. 

Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global health crisis, and new drugs are urgently needed. 

APExModel will establish a set of experimentally-grounded design principles that can aid the development of safer and more effective AMPs. This will be done by developing and applying a new computational framework that integrates experimental data into simulations. The project will also provide: 1) better understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern how AMPs self-assemble in solution, a key factor for their stability and activity; 2) a novel simulation methodology that can accurately model AMPs interacting with cell membranes by using experimental small-angle scattering data to guide the simulations; and 3) insights on the action mechanisms of different AMPs and how they disrupt bacterial membranes.

The most critical R&D challenge is the development of this new simulation methodology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide access to dynamics at atomic resolution, but limitations in simulation timescale and accuracy may compromise the agreement with experiments. Current integrative approaches are limited to systems with spherical symmetry and cannot adequately model the flat, patch-like membrane used in most MD simulations of AMP-membrane studies. This project will overcome this limitation, adding a capability that is currently missing in the field.

Combining expertise from chemistry, pharmacy, and physics, this interdisciplinary project will produce a new open-source simulation tool and the fundamental knowledge required to establish design principles for AMPs.

jobs.description:
The Research Department of Statistics Norway invites applications for a two-year fixed-term position in economics, funded by the Research Council of Norway through "Match effects and matchmaking in education" (MatchEd, project no. 358940). The position is based in Oslo, Norway, with an anticipated starting date of September 1, 2027.  The Research Department conducts economic research using extensive Norwegian administrative data. The department has an established group of researchers working in applied microeconomics, including the economics of education, and close connections with the University of Oslo and the international research community.  About the project  MatchEd explores how the assignment of students to schools, programs, and tracks affects academic outcomes, motivation, and equality of opportunity. Beyond estimating whether some schools or programs benefit particular students more than others (match effects), the project aims to identify the mechanisms behind this heterogeneity, and to translate these insights into evidence-based guidance for designing fairer and more effective assignment systems. The project exploits centralized admission systems (e.g., deferred acceptance with priority-based cutoffs) linked to population-wide registers.  The project is led by Edwin Leuven (Statistics Norway and the University of Oslo) and Sturla Løkken (Statistics Norway).  
Job descriptionThe successful candidate will conduct empirical research using Norwegian administrative data and collaborate with other project members on research papers intended for publication in international economics journals. The position provides opportunities to pursue original research within the scope of the project, with no teaching obligations.   Qualifications
Applicants will be evaluated primarily on research potential, the quality of their research, and the relevance of their interests to the project.  Candidates should have:  

• A PhD in economics or a closely related field, completed by the starting date. Candidates who expect to complete their PhD before taking up the position are welcome to apply. 
• Strong training in applied microeconometrics, particularly causal inference.  
• Experience working with and analyzing individual-level microdata.  
• The ability to conduct independent research and collaborate effectively with other researchers.

• Membership in Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens pensjonskasse, SPK).

Letters of Recommendation may either be uploaded as part of the application or sent directly by the referee to Sturla A. Løkken (sturla.lokken@ssb.no) or Edwin Leuven (edwin.leuven@econ.uio.no). We may conduct background checks and verify submitted documents when relevant.

jobs.occupation: Frequentis - Technical Solution Consultant – Digital Tower ATM
jobs.description:
Help shape the technology behind safe and reliable air traffic operations.

At Frequentis, we develop technology that supports some of the world's most critical operations. Now we're looking for an experienced Technical Solution Consultant to play a key role in ongoing Digital Tower programmes.

In this position, you'll help turn the operational needs of air traffic controllers into technical solutions that work in practice. From defining requirements and shaping system design to integration, testing and final acceptance, you'll contribute to ensuring that complex systems perform as intended.

You'll work in an international environment alongside air traffic professionals, systems engineers, developers, suppliers and project teams. This is an opportunity to take real technical ownership and make a visible contribution to the future of air traffic management.

Your role

As Technical Solution Consultant, you'll connect operational requirements with technical implementation. You'll help create clarity across complex systems, identify dependencies and ensure that solutions are properly verified before entering operational use.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Translating operational and customer needs into clear, structured and testable requirements.

• 
Contributing to solution architecture, system design and technical decisions.

• 
Coordinating system interfaces, integrations and technical dependencies.

• 
Developing test strategies, test cases and acceptance criteria.

• 
Planning and supporting verification, validation, Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) and Site Acceptance Tests (SAT).

• 
Following up technical risks, deviations and documentation throughout the delivery process.

• 
Working closely with customers, air traffic controllers and international technical teams.

What we're looking for

We believe you have solid experience with complex technical systems, within Air Traffic Management (ATM.

You bring practical experience in several of the following areas:

• 
Experience with Digital Tower or ATM technology including Remote Tower solutions, A-SMGCS, camera and video systems, surveillance solutions, control-room interfaces, simulators, SESAR projects or operational safety assessments.

• 
Requirements engineering and systems engineering.

• 
Solution architecture and system integration.

• 
Verification, validation, testing and technical acceptance.

• 
Translating operational workflows into technical requirements and system behaviour.

• 
System Integration and Transition

• 
Technical documentation, traceability and risk management.

• 
Air Traffic Controller experience is a plus.

You have a relevant bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, aviation, systems engineering, IT or a related field. Substantial relevant experience may compensate for formal education.

Excellent written and spoken English is required. A Scandinavian language is an advantage.

You don't need to have held a specific job title. What matters is your ability to take technical ownership and guide complex solutions from requirements through integration, verification and accepted delivery as well as experience in working in matrix organisations.

Why Frequentis?

At Frequentis, your work contributes directly to the safety and reliability of air traffic operations.

You'll join an international technology environment where you can:

• 
Make a meaningful impact: Work on safety-critical solutions used in real operational environments.

• 
Take technical ownership: Influence system design, integration and how solutions are verified and accepted.

• 
Collaborate internationally: Work with experienced specialists, customers and operational stakeholders across the ATM industry.

Develop your expertise: Build experience across ATM operations, solution architecture, systems engineering and verification.

Grow professionally: Explore longer-term opportunities towards roles such as Lead Systems Engineer, Solution Architect or Design Authority.

Stig Aulid+47 915 16 107stig@cruit.no

jobs.occupation: Marketing Manager Nordics
jobs.description:
Turn customer insight into growth across the Nordics
Monil builds virtual fencing technology that makes it easier for farmers to manage livestock on pasture. Our collars and app give farmers a real-time view of their animals and more flexibility in how they graze. Founded in Norway in 2022 by engineers from Teledyne FLIR, Silicon Labs and Cognite, Today, thousands of farmers around the world use Monil to manage their livestock on pasture.

The opportunity
The Nordics are Monil’s home market and a key region for growth. As our Marketing Manager Nordics, you’ll own the regional marketing strategy, budget and lead the work to generate demand and support sales growth across the region. You’ll focus on Norway and Sweden today and help shape how we enter other Nordic markets as we grow.

You’ll get close to farmers to understand what drives their buying decisions, where they hesitate and what helps them get started. You’ll use those insights to build demand, generate qualified leads for Sales and drive purchases through our online store.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll set the plan, decide where to invest and lead campaigns from brief to launch. You’ll work closely with our Nordic Sales and Farmer Success teams, central specialists in performance marketing, content, web, product marketing, brand and PR, and external agencies and partners. You’ll bring the right people into each project and own the priorities and results.

What you’ll be responsible for
Regional strategy and performance

• 
Build regional marketing plans, set targets and forecasts, and own the campaign calendar and budget.

• 
Track and report results, test new approaches and shift investment toward the channels and activities that deliver the strongest return.

Customer insight and messaging

• 
Bring together insights from farmers, Sales, market research and competitors to identify buying drivers, barriers to adoption and opportunities for growth.

• 
Turn those insights into locally relevant messaging, pricing and promotion recommendations, and clear briefs for specialists and agencies.

Campaigns, launches and visibility

• 
Lead regional campaigns, product launches, trade shows, demo days, webinars, partnerships and events from planning through delivery.

• 
Select and work with PR agencies to earn coverage in relevant media.

• 
Brief specialists and agencies, review creative work and approve materials for local markets.

Website, online store and lead generation

• 
Set regional priorities for website localisation, customer journeys, conversion improvements, newsletters and CRM communications.

• 
Work with the web team to improve how customers buy through the online store and how prospective customers connect with Sales.

• 
Analyse performance by channel and across the funnel, and work with Sales to understand which leads convert and where to improve.

What you’ll bring
• 
Experience owning a marketing strategy, budget and measurable business results for a market or region. We’re ideally looking for around 5–7 years of relevant experience.

• 
Hands-on experience across campaigns, paid and digital channels, PR, trade shows and events, websites, CRM and email marketing.

• 
Examples of how you’ve turned customer and market insight into clear priorities, messaging and campaigns.

• 
Strong commercial and analytical judgement. You can connect marketing decisions to lead quality, conversion and return on investment.

• 
Experience taking campaigns, launches or trade shows from planning through delivery.

• 
The ability to bring specialists and agencies together around a clear brief and keep work moving without direct reporting lines.

• 
A good eye for concepts, copy and design. You give clear feedback and are comfortable writing copy yourself when needed.

Fluency in Norwegian or Swedish, with a good understanding of the other language and professional proficiency in English.

• 
Relevant education in marketing, economics or business development, or equivalent practical experience.

• 
Willingness to travel for trade shows, demo days and customer visits in rural areas.

You’re curious about how farmers make decisions, comfortable making trade-offs and motivated by seeing the results of your work.

It’s a plus if you have

• 
Experience marketing to farmers, working in agriculture or agtech, or introducing customers to a new product category.

• 
Experience marketing hardware and subscriptions through both e-commerce and sales-led channels.

• 
A bachelor’s degree or equivalent in economics or engineering.

How we work
We keep things simple, move quickly and learn by testing. You’ll have room to challenge how we do things, try new ideas and adjust priorities based on what you learn. You’ll work closely with colleagues across Marketing, Sales, Farmer Success, Product and Finance.

What we offer
• 
Ownership of the strategy, budget and results in a key growth region for Monil.

• 
A direct link between your work and the leads, sales and growth it generates.

• 
The freedom to choose where to focus, with the opportunity to shape how Monil grows across the Nordics.

An ambitious team that makes decisions quickly and builds technology to make livestock farming easier, more efficient and more sustainable.

jobs.occupation: Senior UX/Service Designer in Oda Systems
jobs.description:
The opportunity
You'll design the tools that get groceries onto millions of doorsteps: not what shoppers see, but the systems used by people working in logistics operations at our fulfillment centers.

Oda’s mission is to build the world’s most efficient retail system, so people have space for life. A huge part of that is our sophisticated fulfillment and delivery system, designed and built entirely by us. It packs and delivers nearly half a million items every day to around 80.000 homes and businesses across Norway and Sweden. What we’ve built is second-to-none in the world when it comes to efficiency, and it’s held together by internal tools and processes that make the jobs of operators and drivers easy, fast, ergonomic, and smooth. That's where you come in.

You'll work in close collaboration with our colleagues in both Norway and at our sister company Mathem in Stockholm, and you’ll help us on the path to launching Oda Systems in new markets as we find customers who want to work with us to bring the most efficient solution for online groceries to more parts of the world.

The role
Service/UX designers play a major part in the design of our processes and tooling. Great processes are as much about ergonomics, workflow, physical space, team structures, and incentives as they are about screens. You’ll get the chance to not only work on software solutions but also consider how digital experiences should best interact with hardware/machinery, the physical space they’re situated in, and last but not least the operator routines around them. That combination is what makes logistics design at Oda different from most UX roles: you're never just designing a screen, you're designing a multi-dimensional workflow.

You’ll join the Delivery team within Oda’s Logistics platform, which is responsible for everything that happens out on the road. You’ll design the best possible experience for employees working with everything from capacity and route planning to traffic coordination, delivering groceries to customers, and leaders following up drivers and operations. While we’re happy with today’s processes, we’re not satisfied: there is a ton to be done to make things more efficient, more automated, and smarter, so that we have even better control over capacity, drivers have a better workday, and customers get their food on time and in full.

You'll work embedded in a cross-functional team, closely collaborating with other disciplines – Product Management, Engineering, Data and Insight, and Logistics development. This is a hands-on, office-based role. You'll be at our Fulfillment Center in Lier regularly, and at our Tøyen office most of the week (most of the team is at Tøyen at least 3 days a week). You’ll use AI actively in your processes, and contribute to driving agentic UX forwards.

What you'll do in Oda
• 
Lead big projects from start to finish: own them from the initial idea through concept, design, prototyping, implementation, testing, and follow-up after launch, working closely with your product team, as well as stakeholders in Logistics. You should feel comfortable putting on the PM hat and driving projects.

• 
Conduct UX research and data analysis: observe what’s going on in operations, run workshops with your team and stakeholders, look at the data, gather feedback in operations.

• 
Communicate and present your work to peers as well as stakeholders, showing your process, and the impact of your designs.

• 
Map and model complex, systemic workflows.

• 
Design user interfaces and build prototypes. You don’t have to be a pixel perfectionist, but you will draw screens. Prototype in Figma, or directly in code – whatever’s the fastest way to test an idea, with room to ship and test changes in production alongside developers.

• 
Work closely with teammates and stakeholders all the way from ideation to roll-out, rather than handing off at the end of a solo-design process.

• 
Contribute to setting the direction of the Delivery team, which determines its own projects based on company strategy

• 
Work with other designers to spar, give feedback, and build a stronger design community across Oda.

What we're looking for 🌟
• 
At least 8 years of experience in UX, interaction, or service design, in-house or agency, with a portfolio showing full ownership from insight to shipped product

• 
A full-stack design attitude: insight, concept, structure, and visual design, without waiting for handovers. Being open to being hands-on both on the warehouse floor and in our codebase.

• 
Very solid fundamentals in product sense and design: demonstrated insight-centric process, root cause analysis, work framed in desired outcomes, ability to distill complexity.

• 
Speed over perfection: You understand the importance of shipping fast, learning, and iterating over polishing a "perfect" blueprint. You leverage the advantage we have with having short feedback loops with our end-users.

• 
A track record of driving process change: not just shipping a solution, but bringing the operators who'll use it along with you.

• 
You already use AI as part of your own design process: you're genuinely interested in an AI-enhanced product development workflow, not just AI features bolted onto Figma.

• 
Fluent English. Intermediate Norwegian or Swedish is a strong plus, since you'll be working directly with traffic coordinators, drivers, and leaders on-site.

• 
Previous logistics experience is a plus, not a requirement.

What we offer 🚀
• 
A flexible schedule built around a healthy work-life balance.

• 
Modern, empowered product teams: democratized data access, good tools, a sustainable pace. We ship, and you will immediately see the impact of your work.

• 
A team that's actively working AI into both design and development, not just talking about it, and genuinely open to designers who want to prototype or write code.

• 
A design community across all Oda teams: UX design, Service design, Digital design, UX research, Content design, and Graphic design.

• 
A culture that values kindness, transparency, and taking action over process for its own sake.

• 
A modern office at Tøyen with an amazing subsidized canteen by Naked Lunch, bike parking, and a great rooftop terrace.

You'll be working with people who are ambitious about logistics in a way most designers never get to be. Come build the future with us!

Oda is committed to being an inclusive community, cultivating diversity, equity, and belonging into our everyday workplace culture. When hiring for our team, we welcome the unique contributions that people can add with different cultural backgrounds, ethnicity, race, gender, gender identity and expression, nationality, age, languages spoken, color, religion, disability, sexual orientation, education and beliefs. If you have a disability such as a hearing, visual impairment or any other neurodivergent need that requires accommodating during the hiring process, please let us know in advance. You can do this by contacting the job owner or hiring manager.

Please apply latest November 29th.

We look forward to hearing from you! 💛

Om arbeidsgiveren:
Oda is the leading online grocery retailer in Norway, but as a company, we’re first and foremost an ambitious tech and logistics company - not a classic retailer. We’re one of the fastest-growing startups in the Nordics, working with huge, complex challenges to make the lives of our customers simpler and easier. Want to join us?

Our goal is to create the world's most efficient retail system. Through smart work, passionate customer focus and our own technology we make a difference in the lives of thousands of customers and change society for the better through a completely re-imagined value chain for grocery shopping.

Our customers save more than 60 hours a year, time we believe can be better spent than going to the store. Our effective value chain and logistics save society tonnes of food waste each year and our distribution network replace almost 13,000 individual trips by car to the grocery store each year.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in cell biology
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a full-time position as Associate Professor in cell biology at the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology, Department of Biosciences, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, University of Oslo.

The Department of Biosciences seeks an active researcher with a strong publication record within cell biology. The successful applicant should be on an upward trajectory and have strong potential to develop and execute research projects at a high international level. The research should address fundamental questions in cell biology using animal- or plant-based systems and create synergies with current research in the section and department. 

Research in the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology includes physiological adaptations to extreme conditions, comparative immunology, muscle physiology, neural mechanisms of learning and memory in health and disease, plant signalling and development, cellular and molecular mechanisms of disease including stress signalling, hormone action and cancer biology, as well as intracellular membrane trafficking, organelle dynamics, and mechanisms regulating cell migration and organization. The research groups develop and apply advanced technologies including live imaging, molecular tools and gene engineering, omics technologies and bioinformatics.

The Department of Biosciences is organized into four research sections; Section for Physiology and Cell biology (FYSCELL), Section for Environmental and marine biology (EMB), Section for, Ecology, Biodiversity, and Evolution (EBE), and Section for Molecular Biology, Biochemistry and Bioinformatics (MBB). The research at the department focuses on fundamental biological processes from the molecular and cellular level to the population and ecosystem level. The department has recently moved into the new Life Science Building, which brings together researchers and students from chemistry, pharmacy, biosciences and laboratory medicine and provides state-of-the-art research infrastructure. The department provides access to advanced research infrastructure, including state-of-the-art core facilities, field stations, and specialized platforms that support interdisciplinary life science research across multiple disciplines.
Your main tasks will be
• Develop and lead an internationally competitive research programme in cell biology, using animal- or plant-based systems and taking advantage of existing infrastructure and common research facilities.
• Secure external research funding and establish or contribute to national and international research collaborations and initiatives.
• Carry out research-based teaching in cell biology and molecular biology at bachelor´s, master´s and PhD levels, including laboratory-based courses and supervise master’s and PhD students.
• Contribute to the academic development of the section and department through collegial activities, scientific leadership, and administrative duties.What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications:

• Completed PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in cell biology or a related field, with a strong scientific track record within cell biology
• Documented experience in securing external research funding.
• Applicants must document academic qualifications in cell biology equivalent to an Associate Professor position. Scientific qualifications will be given significant weight, with particular emphasis on the quality and extent of scientific output within cell biology over the last five years, as well as experience with modern experimental research methods and techniques.
• The successful applicant must be able to carry out research-based teaching in cell and molecular biology at bachelor, master and PhD levels including laboratory-based courses and supervise Master and PhD students.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe their qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time
• A researching approach
• A collegial attitude and practice
• Applicants who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
• The successful candidate must demonstrate mastery of both English and one of the Scandinavian languages as working languages, in order to be able to teach and otherwise be able to participate in all functions the position may involve. Candidates who do not have sufficient mastery of a Scandinavian language (B2 level) at the time of appointment, will be required attain B2 level proficiency in Norwegian within three years of employment.
Desired qualifications:

• Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. Experience in scientific and administrative management is an advantage.
• International research networks, outreach activities, collegiality, and the ability to foster a positive working environment will be considered in the evaluation.
• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience in utilizing advanced research infrastructure such as those available at the Department of Biosciences and the University of Oslo, and the ability to contribute to their further development, is an advantage.What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive and productive research environment
• Networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate should have an international profile consistent with to the above criteria. The candidate will be selected based on documented qualifications and the fit and expertise to strengthen and create synergies with the research profiles of the section and department.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Associate Professor (position code 1011) in salary range NOK from 750 000 - to 850 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, two % is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund. We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at  UiO's policy for diversity, equality and inclusion.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues; could you be the next one?

We will do our best to meet your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (in Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (in Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Application letter
• Research plan (up to 5 pages) describing the applicant’s scientific vision and ambitions and how the proposed research will strengthen or create synergies with ongoing research activities in the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology and the Department of Biosciences.
• Detailed CV, including education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative and management experience, project acquisition and coordination experience, and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of educational certificates, PhD diploma, transcript of records
• Complete list of scientific publications and academic merits and awards.
• Full text of up to 10 selected scientific publications the applicant wishes to include in the evaluation
• A document discussing the importance, interrelation, and relevance of the selected papers for this position
• Educational portfolio of 3–6 pages documenting educational competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own teaching practice and view of learning is anchored in the SoTL framework (focus on student learning, development over time, a researching approach and a collegial attitude and practice) 
• Documentation of experience in obtaining external research funding and fundraising experience.
• List of reference persons: 2–3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
As a general rule an interview will be used in the appointment process, usually supplemented with a trial teaching session.
