jobs.occupation: Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWHqR5i1FHE&feature=youtu.beAbout the Job
The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU Gjøvik has a vacancy for a Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems. 

The position is for an intended period of 24 months and is part of SAFE – Secure Anti-Fraud Excellence Center, funded by Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark and SpareBank 1 Østlandet in collaboration with NTNU and industry partners.The researcher will be a key member of WP1 and lead its socio-technical root cause analysis of financial fraud, hosted at CCIS, NTNU Gjøvik. WP1 examines vishing and safe-account fraud from both the attacker and the victim perspective and a proposed extension to investment fraud. It distinguishes technical authentication and payment confirmation from legally valid consent.

The research reconstructs how fraud unfolds across channels, while focusing detection and intervention on evidence actually visible to the bank between customer authentication and payment authorisation. Off-bank calls, screen sharing and remote-access activities are described where case sources support them, but are not assumed to be observable by the bank.

The work draws on public decisions of Finansklagenemnda, court judgments, and anonymised or otherwise lawfully accessible cases from SAFE’s banking partners. Results feed into cognitive experiments (WP2), detection research (WP3), scientific publications and a policy white paper.Center for Cyber and Information Security (CCIS) at NTNU will host the SAFE Project.Your immediate leader is head of department.
Duties of the position
• Build a systematically coded corpus of fraud cases from public decisions and lawfully accessible bank material, using a shared template and a cross-channel timeline.
• Develop evidence-based fraud scripts for vishing and safe-account fraud and, subject to scope confirmation, investment fraud, including interim inputs for WP2.
• Map each fraud stage, the channels involved, signs of real-time guidance, and what is actually observable by the bank between authentication and payment authorisation.
• Identify legitimate customer activities with similar bank-visible patterns, to support realistic false-alarm testing without using victim characteristics as automatic detection features.
• Study intervention points and fraudster adaptation, including cases where the bank suspects fraud but the customer rejects warnings; help plan a tabletop session with a banking partner.
• Analyse legal, ethical and governance conditions for collecting, using and sharing fraud-related signals, including privacy, bank confidentiality and interbank cooperation.
• Examine the conditions for transaction warnings, delays, refusals and escalation, with attention to customer consent, liability and loss allocation.
• Assess payee verification and, in investment-fraud cases, checks of providers against Finanstilsynet’s register and market warnings; distinguish these from bank-account verification.
• Provide fraud scripts and realistic look-alike scenarios to WP2 and observability findings, intervention points and lawful-signal constraints to WP3.
• Prepare WP1 deliverables, scientific publications and a policy white paper, and present findings to the SAFE Advisory Board and project partners.
• Contribute, where relevant, to SAFE continuing education (EVU), project reporting and research proposal development.Required selection criteria
• A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) or a PhD in information security, socio-technical systems, criminology, information systems, law and technology, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience with systematic analysis of qualitative material, such as case files, legal decisions, interviews or incident reports, using a coding scheme or structured method.
• Knowledge of social engineering and fraud in digital channels, such as vishing, authorised push payment fraud or investment fraud.
• Understanding of digital banking and payment processes, including authentication, payment initiation and customer interaction channels.
• Ability to recognise legal, ethical and data-protection questions and work with relevant specialists on their implications for fraud prevention research.
• Reading comprehension of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language sufficient to analyse Norwegian case material and legal decisions.
• Good written and spoken English and the ability to prepare clear, well-structured research reports.Preferred selection criteria
• A PhD in a relevant field, or research experience after completion of the master’s degree.
• Experience in applied research projects involving banks, financial crime specialists or regulatory and legal experts.
• Experience in crime script analysis, situational crime prevention, socio-technical analysis, or process and threat modelling.
• Knowledge of Norwegian or EU rules on payment services, data protection, bank confidentiality or financial crime prevention.
• Experience in fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, compliance or incident handling in the financial sector.
• Experience in planning and facilitating interviews, workshops or tabletop exercises with practitioners.
• Relevant scientific publications or reports on fraud, cybercrime or socio-technical security.
• Skills in structuring and analysing data, for example using Python, R or NVivo.
• Spoken Norwegian or another Scandinavian language for cooperation with partner banks.Personal characteristics
• Highly motivated for applied and collaborative research with financial-sector partners.
• Analytical, structured and precise in the handling of research evidence and sources.
• Discreet and reliable in handling confidential case material and working across disciplines.
• Self-driven, communicative and able to deliver to agreed deadlines.
• Personal suitability will be emphasized.We offer
• Exciting and stimulating research tasks in a strong international academic environment
• Active collaboration with leading industrial and research partners in Norway and abroad.
• A professional and inclusive work environment.
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Employee benefits at NTNUSalary and conditions
As a researcher (code 1108/1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 580 000– NOK 750 000 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU. 

The intended appointment period is 24 months. Starting date at the latest: 1st April 2027.  Please note that loss of external funding is considered equivalent to loss of work assignments, see §19 (1) of the public Employees act. In the event of dismissal by the employer, the notice period is according to §22 (1) of the Public Employers Act. 

It is a prerequisite that you can be present at and accessible to the institution on a daily basis. After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.
About the application
Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. 

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in  English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your application must include:

• Motivation letter describing your interest in SAFE and socio-technical research on financial fraud (maximum one page).
• CV and relevant certificates.
• Transcripts, diplomas and diploma supplements for completed degrees (BSc, MSc and, where applicable, PhD).
• Master’s thesis or equivalent substantial research work, plus up to three other relevant scientific publications or reports.
• A short statement (1–2 pages) explaining your experience with case-based analysis and how you would map a fraud scenario across channels, distinguish bank-visible evidence from external context, and identify legal or ethical constraints.
• Names and contact information of at least two referees.
It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for  documentation of your competence.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.
General information
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.   

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.  

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. 

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. 

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Prof. Stewart James Kowalski, email: stewart.kowalskntnu.no . If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact HR Katrine Rennan, e-mail: katrine.rennan@ntnu.no .

Application deadline: 31.12.2026.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in maps and models for nature in land-use planning
jobs.description:
Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL) has a vacancy for a PhD Research Fellow in maps and models for nature in land-use planning
About the position:

The PhD Research Fellow will join the Landscape, Ecology and Climate research group at the Department of Civil Engineering and Environmental Sciences, at the Sogndal campus. The position is funded through the national research center Landfutures, as part of its research area "Maps and models". The position is a fixed-term, four year position with 25 % career-enhancing work at the department. The candidate will be enrolled in the PhD program Responsible Innovation and Regional Development at HVL.  Planned start date is Q1 of 2027.
About the PhD project/ work tasks:
About LandfuturesLandfutures is an eight-year research center for sustainable land and nature use (2026– 2034), funded by the Research Council of Norway. The center is led by Western Norway Research Institute and run jointly with Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, the Norwegian Mapping Authority (Kartverket), the Institute of Transport Economics, Nordland Research Institute, Ruralis, the Norwegian Computing Center and the Basque Center for Climate Change. Landfutures focuses on interests, values and practices in planning, with special attention to the regional level, and works closely with county authorities, county governors and municipalities.

Background and research needLand-use change is the main driver of biodiversity loss in Norway, and most decisions about land use outside protected areas are made in municipal land-use planning. At the core of these decisions is usually a map: which areas are most valuable for biodiversity, and where would development do the least harm? Yet mapping of nature is patchy, and although new nationwide data products such as the planned "Naturkart" are on the way, data alone do not tell a planner what to do. Municipalities can calculate the greenhouse-gas emissions of land-use change, but biodiversity has no currency comparable to tonnes of carbon dioxide Project-level methods such as "Naturkompasset" are emerging, but no spatially explicit tool supports strategic, plan-level choices about where to build. Systematic conservation planning offers  principles for such a tool: explicit targets, complementary areas, minimum cost and transparent trade-offs. Mature software exists (e.g. prioritizr, Zonation, Marxan), but the approach is hardly used in Norwegian planning. Different targets, data and methods can also point to different places on the map, and how far professionals agree on where nature matters most is an open question. 

Possible research directionsThe PhD project addresses one overarching question: How can maps and models give robust, transparent recommendations that professionals can agree on, about where to build and where to safeguard nature? We see three broad areas in which the thesis can contribute. The examples are meant to show the range of possibilities, not a fixed work plan. 

1. Practice – how plans and assessment methods treat nature today. What do existing planning documents and assessment methods actually map, prioritize and assume? Examples: how municipal biodiversity plans ("kommunedelplaner for naturmangfold") reflect principles from conservation biology and landscape ecology, such as complementarity and connectivity; or how new methods for assessing nature loss in development projects, such as "Naturkompasset", are structured and used.

2. Tools – spatial prioritization and how sensitive the answers are. Which planning needs can be formulated as spatial optimization problems, and how robust are the resulting recommendations? Examples: using systematic conservation planning at county scale to support plan revision ("planvask" – reviewing outdated zoning for development) or coordination across municipal borders; testing how much priority maps or impact scores change with different input data, criteria or assumptions about ecosystem condition.

3. Uncertainty and agreement – where experts and data diverge, and where new knowledge pays off. How large is professional disagreement about priority areas, and where would better data change the decision? Examples: how similar the priority maps are when independent groups of experts solve the same planning task; or identifying locations where additional field surveys in environmental impact assessments would be most likely to change a planning decision. 

The thesis will be article-based, comprising 3–4 scientific papers. Their exact scope, cases and methods will be developed together with the supervisors, and we expect the candidate to shape at least one of them from their own ideas (see Application below). User partners in Landfutures offer opportunities to work with real planning processes and cases. 

Research environmentThe PhD Research Fellow will be part of the Landscape, Ecology and Climate research group in Sogndal, an interdisciplinary group of ecologists and social scientists. The supervision team is Associate Professor Julien Vollering and Professor Inger Auestad, with the opportunity to involve additional supervisors where needed. Through Landfutures, the candidate will work with research partners such as the Norwegian Mapping Authority and the Norwegian Computing Center. User partners include seven county authorities, four county governors, and municipalities through the Norwegian Association of Local and Regional Authorities (KS). The center is recruiting four PhD candidates and three postdocs with different disciplinary backgrounds, and there are opportunities for exchange with complementary PhD projects within and outside Landfutures. The research fellow will recieve a fixed annual stipend to cover necessary expenses, such as participation in conferences/workshops/training or purchase of services/licenses/equipment.

Teaching duties would likely be in courses such as landscape ecology, GIS, or spatial planning.
Qualifications:
Criteria for appointment to the position of Phd Research Fellow are regulated in Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.

Required qualifications:

• A Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in ecology, conservation biology, physical or human geography, environmental or natural resource management, climate change management, land-use planning, landscape architecture, or a closely related field
• Grade B or better on the Master’s thesis and grade C or better on average in the Master’s degree (ECTS scale or equivalent)
• Documented experience with GIS and spatial data analysis
• Documented experience with R or another programming language for data analysis, such as Python
• Minimum B1 level in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language, and minimum B2 level in English (CEFR)
The following qualifications will be considered advantageous:

• Familiarity with Norwegian land-use planning or nature management, for example through work experience
• Experience with spatial prioritization or statistical modeling of spatial data
• Experience with R specifically (if your programming experience is in another language)
• B2 level or higher in Norwegian and C1 level or higher in English (CEFR)
We are looking for someone who: 

• is curious, analytical and comfortable working with varied map data
• works well both independently and together with researchers and practitioners from other disciplines
Applicants should explicitly address the qualifications listed above in their application, and provide documentation supporting them. 

Admission to the PhD programme

An application for admission to the programme should be submitted only after employment has been secured. Normally, an application for admission to the PhD programme must be submitted within 3 months of the start date. See Section 2-4 of the Regulations for the Degree of PhD at HVL. The research fellow must be admitted to the PhD programme no later than 3 months after the commencement of their employment. Further information about the PhD programme can be found at https://www.hvl.no/en/research/phd-programmes/.

Career plan

The person appointed must, in conjunction with the department, prepare a career plan that specifies the competences the fellow is to acquire. Competence goals must be set for both the doctoral work and any other career-enhancing work that is added to the position. The fellow will have access to career guidance. Other career-enhancing work may, for example, include teaching and teaching-related work, acquiring Norwegian language skills, contributions to research communities, collaboration with public or private actors, and more.

Background check

For available positions, HVL conducts background checks on applicants in collaboration with an external supplier, to verify information that appears from available documents. Background checks are always carried out with the candidate's consent, and employment in these positions requires a completed background check.
Application procedure:
Applications will be evaluated by an expert panel of three members.

Applicants are asked to submit their application and CV online. Please use the link “Apply for this job” (“Søk stillingen”).

The following documentation should be uploaded as an attachment to the online application: 

• Research Sketch (max. 1 page, 500 words) describing a paper you would like to pursue within the research area: the question, why it matters, and how it could be answered. The sketch will be assessed on relevance, originality and feasibility. It is not binding – its purpose is to show how you think. The sketch may be written in English or Norwegian; references do not count toward the page limit.
• Diplomas and certificates
• Master Thesis
• If any, copies of selected academic publications (no more than 15)
• A CV with a complete list of academic publications
Applicants should indicate which publications or parts of publications should be given special consideration in the evaluation. If the documents submitted are not in a Scandinavian language or in English, the applicants must submit certified translations of these. The transcripts must specify the topics, the course works, and the grades at the bachelor`s and master`s degree levels.

Applicants with a degree from a country other than Norway, need to attach a certified translation of the diploma and transcripts of grades to English or a Scandinavian language, in addition to the original documents, if the original is not in any of these languages. It is required that the applicant encloses a recognition document showing that their degree is equivalent to a Norwegian bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD. You can read more about applying for recognition of foreign higher education here.

The Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) offers an automatic recognition document for certain degrees from selected countries. If the applicant’s degree is covered by the automatic recognition, it will be sufficient to attach this document. Read more about automatic recognition here.

As the HK-dir application process may take some time it is recommended to apply to HK-dir as soon as possible. If you have not received a recognition document from HK- dir within the application deadline, please enclose documentation from HK-dir showing that they have received your application.

Applicants should note that the evaluation will be based on the documentation submitted electronically via Jobbnorge within the submission deadline. The applicants are responsible for ensuring that all the documentation is submitted before the closing date. It is of utmost importance that all publications to be considered in the evaluation are uploaded as an attachment with the application, since these are sent electronically to the expert panel. Applications cannot be sent by e-mail or to individuals at the college.
General information:
The appointment will be made in accordance with the regulations for State employees Law in Norway ("Lov om statens ansatte"). Organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities associated with the position must be expected.

State employment shall reflect the multiplicity of the population at large to the highest possible degree. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences therefore aims to achieve a balanced age and gender composition and the recruitment of persons with diverse backgrounds.

Information about the applicants may be made public even though the applicant has requested not to be named in the list of applicants. The applicant will be notified if his/her request is not respected.

Short-listed applicants will be called in for an interview. 

Employment is on condition that you are granted a work and residence permit (considered individually).

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to the regulation for export control system. The regulation will be applied in the processing of the applications.
Salary:
• Good occupational pension, insurance and loan schemes from The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Exciting academic environment with the possibility of competence enhancement and development
• Opportunities for training within the working hours  
The PhD Research Fellow position is compensated according to position code 1017 Research Fellow, with a starting salary of NOK 568.700,-. Automatic salary progression is provided for up to 4 years, with an annual increase of 3%. 

There is a compulsory 2 % deduction to the pension fund (see http://www.spk.no for more information). The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.
Contacts:
1) Inger Auestad, Professor -  + 47 57676222 / email: inger.auestad@hvl.no

3) Liv Norunn Hamre, Assistant head of department - +47 57676229 / email: liv.hamre@hvl.no
 
2. Julien Vollering, Associate Professor - email: julien.vollering@hvl.no

Om arbeidsgiveren:

With about 16, 500 students, Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is one of the largest higher education institutions in Norway. A broad range of academic programmes are offered at Bachelor, Master and PhD levels, spread out on five campuses Førde, Sogndal, Bergen, Stord og Haugesund.

Our ambition is to build stronger and more solid academic and research environments that will interact nationally and internationally. The aim is to become a recognized actor on the international higher education arena. Increased international cooperation and engagement in externally funded projects will work towards this goal.

The Faculty of Engineering and Science has approximately 370 employees and approximately 3,260 students. The faculty has a broad educational offer at both bachelor's and master's level in engineering and science, as well as two PhD programmes. We cooperate with many national and international research groups, and with national and regional industry partners.

The Department of Civil Engineering and Environmental Sciences has a strong academic and research environment, offering programmes at bachelor’s and master’s levels across our campuses in Sogndal and Bergen. The department has around 900 students and more than 80 staff members and plays a key role in advancing the green transition through research and education in sustainable infrastructure, land use, and nature restoration.

jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i forhistorisk arkeologi
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i forhistorisk arkeologi ved Arkeologisk museum, Avdeling for konservering. Stillingen er ledig fra 1.mars 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder frem til en doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen vil du tilegne deg kunnskaper, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innen forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

Den som ansettes vil bli tatt opp på ph.d.-programmet i Samfunnsvitenskap. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning. 

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.

Stillingen er eksternt finansiert gjennom prosjektet «TRACES: Tracking Rock Art and oChre EnvironmentS», som er finansiert av Norges forskningsråd (NFR).
Forskningstema
TRACES undersøker forhistorisk bruk av oker, teknologi knyttet til bergkunst og samspillet mellom mennesker og miljø i Nord-Norge gjennom forhistorisk tid. Pigmenter og bergmalerier representerer noen av menneskehetens tidligste symbolske uttrykkssystemer og gir innsikt i menneskelig kommunikasjon, identitet og tilknytning gjennom tusenvis av år.

Prosjektets hovedhypotese er at felles teknologiske nettverk bidro til å opprettholde kulturelle og sosiale tradisjoner i perioder med omfattende klimatiske endringer. Sentrale forskningsspørsmål er blant annet:

• Hvilke strategier ble benyttet for anskaffelse av oker, og hvordan var mobilitets- og utvekslingsnettverkene knyttet til oker organisert i forhistorisk Norge?
• Hvordan varierte disse nettverkene over tid og mellom ulike regioner?
• I hvilken grad kan koblinger mellom pigmenter på udaterte bergmalerier og daterte arkeologiske kontekster bidra til å etablere et materialbasert kronologisk rammeverk?
• Hvordan tilpasset forhistoriske jeger-sankergrupper sine teknologiske systemer og symbolske nettverk seg til store miljø- og klimaendringer?
Stipendiatens rolleStipendiaten skal forske på arkeologiske okersamlinger og forhistoriske pigmentteknologier i Norge. Datagrunnlaget vil bli utviklet gjennom studier av museumsamlinger, publisert forskning og grå litteratur, ikke-destruktive spektroskopiske analyser i felt, geokjemiske laboratorieundersøkelser samt eksperimentell rekonstruksjon av forhistoriske malingoppskrifter og pigmentnettverk.

Den som ansettes vil utforske, anvende og kombinere ulike analytiske tilnærminger og metoder, herunder:

• katalogisering av museums-samlinger og gjenstander
• gjennomføring av geokjemiske analyser
• bruk av multivariate statistiske metoder
• planlegging og gjennomføring av workshops innen eksperimentell arkeologi 
Erfaring fra ett eller flere av disse områdene er en fordel. Søkere med erfaring fra arkeometriske analysemetoder, for eksempel SEM-EDS, (p)XRF, XRD, Raman-spektroskopi eller LA-ICP-MS, vil bli foretrukket. Opplæring i relevante metoder vil bli gitt ved behov.

Stipendiaten forventes å utvikle ny kunnskap som bidrar både til egen faglig kompetanseutvikling og til prosjektets samlede målsettinger. Stipendiaten vil inngå som en sentral del av prosjektgruppen og delta aktivt i prosjektets ulike aktiviteter, inkludert møter, workshops, vitenskapelig formidling og publisering.

Det oppfordres også til at stipendiaten gjennomfører et forskningsopphold ved Archaeometry Laboratory ved University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR), USA, i løpet av stipendiatperioden.
Prosjektskisse
Som søker skal du utarbeide en foreløpig prosjektskisse ( 3-5 sider) for et doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor det beskrevne forskningstemaet.

Prosjektskissen skal redegjøre for forskningsproblemstillingen, dens relevans, samt den foreslåtte teoretiske og metodiske tilnærmingen. Skissen vil inngå i kompetansevurderingen.

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. Mal for prosjektskisse finner du her.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha sterk faglig bakgrunn med en femårig mastergrad i arkeologi, konservering, arkeometri, arkeologisk vitenskap, kulturarvvitenskap, geovitenskap, konserveringsvitenskap eller et nært beslektet fagområde, eller tilsvarende kvalifikasjoner som gir grunnlag for opptak til doktorgradsutdanning. Det er en fordel at graden er avlagt nylig.

Karakteren på masteroppgaven og det vektede gjennomsnittet for mastergraden må begge tilsvare karakteren B eller bedre.

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.
 
Vi vil også legge vekt på om du:

• viser høy faglig integritet og en sterk forpliktelse til kvalitet i arbeidet ditt
• er nysgjerrig og motivert for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og tverrfaglig samarbeid
• har et godt forskningspotensial innen fagområdet og de personlige egenskapene som kreves for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• evner å arbeide effektivt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• viser evne til kritisk refleksjon, innovativ tenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, samt arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø
• behersker engelsk godt, både muntlig og skriftlig.Krav til kompetanse i engelsk
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk er påkrevd for deltakelse i doktorgradsprogrammet. Internasjonale søkere må dokumentere dette med gyldig sertifikat fra en av følgende tester: 

• TOEFL - Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT). Minimum resultat: 90 
• IELTS - International English Language Testing Service. Minimum resultat: 6.5 
• Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) og Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) fra Universitetet i Cambridge 
• PTE Academic - Pearson Test of English Academic. Minimum resultat: 62 
Følgende søkere er fritatt fra ovennevnte krav: 

• søkere med ett års fullført universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia, USA 
• søkere med fullført mastergrad med engelsk som undervisningsspråk i et EU-/EØS-land 
• søkere som er fritatt basert på HK-dir sin GSU liste Vi tilbyr
• doktorgradsutdanning ved et universitet med et tydelig samfunnsoppdrag og ambisiøse faglige mål
• et ambisiøst og inkluderende forskningsmiljø. Vi legger vekt på å involvere ansatte på alle nivåer i strategiske beslutninger og fremmer en uformell arbeidskultur med flat organisasjonsstruktur
• gratis norskopplæring dersom du ikke behersker norsk, svensk eller dansk på nivå A2 ved tiltredelse
• tilgang til Lifekeys, en digital tjeneste for mental helse og livskvalitet
• lønn etter Statens lønnsregulativ i stillingskode 1017 stipendiat, for tiden kr 580 000 brutto per år, med lønnsutvikling i ansettelsesperioden. Fra lønnen trekkes lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse på 2 %
• medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse med gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Les mer om ansattgoder og fordeler på uis.no.
Mangfold
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  
Har du spørsmål?
Vil du høre mer om stillingen, ta kontakt med:

Avdelingsleder: Hilde Alette Smedstad Moore, Tlf: 51832688, e-mail: hilde.s.moore@uis.no 

Har du spørsmål vedrørende rekrutteringsprosessen ta kontakt med: 

HR rådgiver: Elin Rødland, Tlf: 51832383, e-mail: elin.rodland@uis.no.
Søknaden
Søk stillingen elektronisk via «Søk stillingen» på denne siden. I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden: 

• prosjektskisse, mal tilgjengelig på våre nettsider
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd
• publikasjoner eller annet relevant forskningsarbeid
• attester og annen dokumentasjon som vurderes relevant for søknaden 
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgrads-utdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden ph.d. ved UiS.

Din kompetanse for stillingen, ut fra dokumentasjon registrert i Jobbnorge, vil bli vurdert av en intern komite. På bakgrunn av komiteens uttalelse vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger vil være en drivkraft i innovasjon og omstilling av samfunnet. Grønn omstilling står sentralt i vår virksomhet, med bærekraft på vei inn i alle studieprogrammer. Våre satsingsområder er energi, helse og velferd og læring for livet. Her kommer du til en arbeidsplass preget av fremragende forskere, yrende studentliv og høy trivsel blant våre 2.000 ansatte. Vi er et åpent universitet, raust og inkluderende, med levende møteplasser for kritisk refleksjon, kunnskapsdeling og konstruktiv debatt. Ett av våre fremste kjennetegn er utstrakt samarbeid med arbeidslivet, både i forskning og utdanning. UiS satser på innovative og fleksible læringsmetoder for våre 12.000 studenter. Universitetet ligger i Norges tredje største byregion med 340.000 innbyggere. Regionen er internasjonal og har et dynamisk arbeidsliv, spennende kulturliv og rik tilgang på naturopplevelser.

Som ansatt får du tilgang til billigere kollektivtransport, trening i arbeidstiden, mulighet for fleksibel arbeidstid og boliglån i Statens pensjonskasse.  

Arkeologisk museum er en tverrfaglig institusjon med oppgaver innenfor forskning, formidling, fornminnevern, konservering samt dokumentasjon og samling. Museet har et vitenskapelig personale med forskere innenfor arkeologi, konservering, ulike naturfag og nyere tids kulturhistorie. Det museumsfaglige personalet dekker flere felter innenfor konservering, naturvitenskapelige laboratorier, fototjenester, arkiv og vitenskapelige samlinger, forvaltningsoppgaver i henhold til Lov om kulturminner, utstillingsproduksjon, grafisk formgivning, skoletjeneste, publikumstilbud og utleievirksomhet. Museet driver et forlag med to serier som er poenggivende i CRIStin. Museet har i dag omlag 80 fast ansatte fordelt på fire fagavdelinger og en administrasjon.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Multi-Omics at Centre for Precision Psychiatry
jobs.description:
About the position
At the Centre for Precision Psychiatry, Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo, we have two full-time 3-year Postdoctoral Research Fellowships available within Novo Nordisk Foundation (NNF) funded projects focused on uncovering mechanistic links between mid-life metabolic trajectories and late onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD).

These positions offer an exciting opportunity for highly motivated researchers to work at the interface of multi-omics, brain and body imaging, and artificial intelligence, contributing to a large-scale Norwegian, UK, and international biobank collaborations aimed at understanding how midlife metabolic dysfunction shifts the risk and timing of AD.

These NNF funded projects collectively aim to uncover the molecular mechanisms linking midlife metabolic trajectories to late-onset AD, and to translate these insights into a novel explainable AI-driven multimodal framework for personalized prediction. The project integrates multi-omics data (genetics, proteomics, metabolomics), brain and body MRI, cognitive assessments, and health registry-linked data from individuals across Norway and the UK.

The Centre for Precision Psychiatry has access to a rich and unique data infrastructure, including large databases of biomarkers, clinical and cognitive variables, genotyping and sequencing data, and MRI brain imaging data from patients with neuropsychiatric and severe mental disorders. In addition, the Centre actively collaborates with major international consortia, including the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC), the ENIGMA consortium, and the European Alzheimer’s Disease DNA BioBank (EADB). The research environment further benefits from access to data from a broad range of national and international studies, including Norwegian population cohorts (e.g., DemGene, HUSK, HUNT, Tromsø study, and MoBa), UK-based cohorts (EPIC-Norfolk, Fenland, and the UK Biobank), the Estonian Biobank, and the ABCD and ADNI studies.
 
The positions are primarily focused on the development and application of statistical and machine learning methods for integrating large-scale longitudinal multi-omics data (proteomics and metabolomics), with clinical and imaging data, and genetics from Norwegian and international biobanks. The postdoctoral fellows will contribute to the following activities: (1) identifying midlife metabolic trajectories that precede neurodegeneration and AD, including metabolic subtyping; (2) linking these trajectories to established neurodegeneration markers, brain and body MRI, and cognition; (3) characterizing gene x environment interactions that shape AD risk and timing; and (4) developing and validating the “AD Avatar” for predicting age of onset.

The successful candidates will work closely with an interdisciplinary research environment including statisticians, geneticists, clinicians, and data scientists, and will conduct research using state-of-the-art secure infrastructure, including the TSD platform at the University of Oslo.

These postdoctoral fellowships are intended to strengthen the candidate’s scientific independence and publication record, and to provide strong qualifications for future academic or research leadership positions within precision medicine, population health, and data-driven neuroscience.

For more information: https://www.med.uio.no/klinmed/english/research/centres/precision-psychiatry/
Main responsibilities
• Analyze and integrate large-scale multi-omics data (affinity-based proteomics and NMR- and mass spectrometry-based metabolomics) from Norwegian and international biobanks, applying time-to-event models and advanced statistical and machine learning methods
• Develop and validate longitudinal models of metabolic trajectories and age-dependent genetic and environmental effects using in-house tools such as FEMA-LONG, and contribute to open-source analytical pipelines
• Apply Mendelian randomization, mediation, colocalization, and genetic overlap analyses (e.g., MiXeR, conjFDR) to investigate causal links between metabolic dysfunction, cardiometabolic disease, and AD-related outcomes
• Contribute to the development of the explainable “AD Avatar” predictive framework, including federated learning across Norwegian and UK-based data infrastructures (TSD, Tryggve, UKB-RAP)
• Collaborate with an interdisciplinary team and international partners in the UK, Sweden, Denmark, Iceland, Estonia, and the USA.
• Prepare and publish high-quality scientific manuscripts and present findings at national and international conferencesQualifications
Required

• A PhD in statistics, mathematics, informatics, genetics, medicine, psychology, or an equivalent field
• Strong programming skills in Python, R, or MATLAB, with emphasis on data analysis and method development
• Solid experience in statistical analysis and data processing using relevant statistical software
• Experience with large-scale human datasets, including multi-omics and/or imaging data
• Experience with tools and pipelines for genetic data analysis (e.g., PLINK, Regenie)
• Excellent proficiency in written and spoken English 
Preferred

• Experience with molecular quantitative trait loci studies, integrating NMR-based metabolomics (Nightingale) or mass spectrometry (Metabolon, Biocrates), and/or affinity-based proteomics data (SomaScan, Olink) with genetic data
• Experience with machine learning for large multimodal datasets and brain image analysis (e.g., FreeSurfer, FSL)
• Experience with computational methods and workflows for handling large-scale multimodal data
• Experience with survival analysis, longitudinal mixed-effects modelling, or clinical risk predictionPersonal skills
• Highly organized, self-driven, and goal-oriented, with strong productivity and attention to detail.
• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary research teams.
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.
We need different perspectives in our work 
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
We offer
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities. 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Postdoctoral Fellow, position code 1352 in salary range NOK 600 000 - 690 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.
 

Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.
Application
Your application should include:

• Application letter
• CV
• A complete list of publications
• Project description
• Transcripts and certificates
• Contact information for 2-3 references
Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
Please note that we are unable to add documentation after the application deadline. As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews. 

No one can be employed for more than one fixed-term period as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the same institution.
 
Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and Guidelines concerning appointment to recruitment positions at UiO. 

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees to secure the rights to all research results and related intellectual property.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

 

The Institute of Clinical Medicine (Klinmed) is one of three institutes under the Faculty. Klinmed is responsible for the Faculty's educational and research activities at Oslo University Hospital and Akershus University Hospital. With about 900 employees spread over approximately 425 man-labour years, Klinmed is the university's largest institute. Our activities follow the clinical activity at the hospitals and are spread across a number of geographical areas.

jobs.occupation: Are you our new Mechanical Designer?
jobs.description:
Join us in shaping the next generation of maritime technology. We are looking for a Mechanical Designer to strengthen our hardware organization and develop robust, functional and manufacturable solutions for maritime applications. In this role, you will turn requirements and ideas into mechanical designs, contributing from early concepts through detailed design, prototyping and production follow-up.

We are looking for someone who combines practical mechanical understanding with an interest in product development. If you enjoy 3D modelling, solving design challenges and working with materials and manufacturing processes—and preferably have an interest in maritime applications—we would love to hear from you.

As a Mechanical Designer, you will develop mechanical parts, assemblies, enclosures and mounting solutions as part of a multidisciplinary team. You will collaborate with hardware engineers, product management, suppliers and production to ensure that design meets requirements for functionality, quality, assembly and serviceability throughout the product lifecycle.

If you enjoy combining creative design with structured engineering and hands-on problem-solving, this role could be a great fit for you.

 

Key accountabilities

• Develop concepts, 3D CAD models and detailed mechanical designs for parts and assemblies.
• Prepare and maintain production drawings, bills of materials and technical documentation, including tolerances and material specifications.
• Select materials, surface treatments and manufacturing methods, considering corrosion resistance, cost, quality and environmental requirements.
• Collaborate with suppliers and production to optimise designs for manufacturing, assembly and serviceability.
• Participate in design reviews, prototype builds and verification testing, following up findings and design improvements.
• Support existing products through mechanical design updates, engineering changes and resolution of production and field issues.
 

This employment may require a pre-employment check procedure in accordance with company security standards, role or site requirements. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment.

This employment requires security clearance by the Norwegian National Security Authority. The successful candidate may start work with limited accesses whilst the clearance is being processed. Please note that this might affect the offer process or employment.

Qualifications and experience

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, or technical college qualification, in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Design, Product Development or a related field. We encourage 2026 graduates to apply.
• Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling and preparation of technical drawings, gained through studies, projects or professional experience.
• Knowledge of dimensioning, geometrical tolerancing (GD&T), tolerance analysis and design for manufacturing and assembly.
• Good English communication, written and verbal.
• Understanding materials, surface treatments and manufacturing processes such as sheet metal fabrication and machining.
• Familiarity with product data or lifecycle management systems (PLM), bills of materials and revision control is an advantage.
• Experience with maritime or industrial equipment, prototyping, mechanical testing or structural analysis is an advantage.

Employer branding experience.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Scholar positions - Department of Finance
jobs.description:
The PhD specialisation
NHH is pleased to announce openings in the PhD specialisation in Finance. Candidates admitted to the PhD programme will receive the title of PhD Research Scholar.

The Department of Finance has 23 faculty members, two-thirds of whom are international. Research at the department spans all major fields of finance, including corporate finance, asset pricing, and financial intermediation. Faculty regularly publish in the top academic journals and are one of the leading finance groups in Europe. The department has an active research seminar series featuring invited top scholars and an internal brown bag seminar series.

The PhD specialisation in Finance gives PhD research scholars the theoretical knowledge and methodological skills necessary to become successful researchers. It combines a one-year intensive course portfolio with ample time to do research and write a dissertation. PhD research scholars work closely with their thesis advisors and receive feedback by presenting their research in internal seminars. The department offers a stimulating research environment and encourages PhD research scholars to participate in its many research activities. We have a strong record of placing graduates in international academic institutions. Research and conference travels are strongly encouraged and funding for these purposes is usually available. The Department of Finance is well connected internationally and is a member of the Nordic Finance Network. Many of our PhD research scholars spend a semester or a year abroad visiting another university. The PhD specialisation in Finance, which has a total of 10 to 12 PhD research scholars, is an important integrated part of the department’s research environment. 

See the department’s website here: Department of Finance | NHH

Start date: August 2027
The PhD programme
The PhD programme at NHH is a four-year fully-funded programme, which combines an intensive course component and research, preparing the school’s graduates for scholarly positions at reputable research institutions and positions in knowledge-intensive organisations both within and outside academia. Former PhD graduates have been hired by renowned institutions such as Harvard University, The University of Sydney’s Business School, University of Amsterdam, University of St. Gallen, Tilburg University, Stockholm School of Economics, Copenhagen Business School, Hanken School of Economics, Norwegian universities and business schools, as well as by government, banking, finance and consulting industries.

The PhD research scholars will be included in a highly stimulating and rewarding research environment, working closely with faculty members and fellow PhD research scholars. PhD research scholars participate actively in faculty and research seminars, as well as in workshops. As part of the position, the PhD research scholars allocate 25% of their time to career promoting work such as teaching assistance. They also receive pedagogical training. The place of work is at NHH in Bergen, where the PhD research scholars will have their own office space at their department.

The PhD programme gives preference to applicants who address research questions that align with the department’s research interests and the available resources for supervision. As the school aspires gender balance and diversity, female applicants will be given preference if applicants are otherwise equally qualified.
NHH offers
• annual salary of NOK 600 000 (equivalent to approximately EUR 55 946 or USD 61 457) pr. August 2027. For particularly well-qualified applicants, a higher salary may be considered. Thereafter annual adjustment of minimum 3%. The salary ensures a fair standard of living in Norway and is subject to Norwegian taxes and benefits, including public health care benefits and pension savings
• career guidance and an individual career development plan
• opportunity to take basic Norwegian language courses
• research funds for travels and funding for conference participation and research stays abroad to build a wider network and strengthen the research of the PhD research scholar
Bergen provides a vibrant cultural scene with easy access to mountains, fjords and a wide range of outdoor activities. The city offers a family-friendly environment and was ranked the best city in Europe for quality of life in Oxford Economics’ 2026 Global Cities Index. Most public services, like healthcare and schools are free in Norway. To explore Norway and the city of Bergen, go to visitnorway.com.
Eligibility requirements
Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements for the PhD programme. Applicants must normally have completed a five-year Master of Science (MSc) degree in Economics and Business Administration or a comparable degree. The average grade must normally correspond to a minimum of B (4.0) in the Norwegian grade system. 

The Department of Finance requires you to demonstrate both an adequate level of academic skills and an adequate level of English language proficiency (unless you are exempt). We accept the following tests:

• GMAT or GRE tests to measure your academic skills
• TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic to measure your English language proficiency
When applying, you are required to upload a copy of your unofficial test scores in Jobbnorge before the deadline. If you are shortlisted, NHH will ask you to give us access to your official test scores without delay.

Exemptions:

• You are waived from the GMAT or GRE tests if you hold a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution.
• You are waived from TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic tests if you are a native English speaker, if you have a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution or if you have a qualifying master’s degree where the language of tuition was English.
For more detailed information about the tests and their minimum scores, please visit our webpage: Admission to the PhD programme| NHH. If you have questions, you may contact phd@nhh.no.
Application requirements
You are required to upload the following documents with your application in Jobbnorge:

• Certificate of your master’s degree or equivalent, including transcripts of records. You need to have completed your master’s degree prior to the starting date for the position. If you have not completed your degree when applying for the position, please attach a transcript of records of the courses and grades that you have completed so far.
• Certificate of your bachelor’s degree or equivalent, including transcripts of records.
• Other relevant certificates or transcripts (e.g. courses completed at the PhD level).
• If the issuing authority of grades and degrees does not use the ECTS grading scale, include an official description of the grading scale used.
• Statement of purpose describing your motivation for applying for this position (250-300 words).
• A research proposal (2000-4000 words). The research proposal should describe the aims, research questions, and motivation of the proposed research. Please note that your research proposal is tentative and often needs adjustments after your acceptance into the programme. 
• Curriculum vitae.
• A list of all publications and/or other documented research activities.   
Please upload the documents in separate files, not combined in one single file.

Letters of recommendation and contact details of references:

Letters of recommendation and/or contact details of references may strengthen your application, but they are not mandatory. If you choose to include letters of recommendations, the references should send their letter of recommendation in PDF format to hr-phd@nhh.no by latest 15 January 2027. Contact details of references may be included in Jobbnorge when you apply. 
General information
For more information on the PhD programme and the submission procedure, please consult the NHH PhD website. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Please note that applicants for the PhD research scholar position do not need to apply separately for admission to the PhD programme.

NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.
 
As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

For questions and inquiries about the NHH PhD programme, please contact phd@nhh.no.

Applications must be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click ‘Apply for this job’. For the English version, go to the menu at the top right side.

Application deadline: 15 January 2027

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Scholar positions - Department of Strategy and Management
jobs.description:
The PhD specialisation
NHH is pleased to announce vacancies in the Department of Strategy and Management. Candidates admitted to the PhD program will receive the title of PhD Research Scholar. The department welcomes applications specialising in several fields of research such as strategy, innovation, management, organizational behaviour, and marketing. The research areas described below represent research opportunities emphasised by the Department, but applications within other relevant research areas are also welcome.

Start date: August 2027Digital Innovation for sustainable GrowthDigital Innovation for sustainable Growth (DIG) is a research center at the Department of Strategy and Management, focusing on sustainable growth and transformation enabled by digital technologies. As a PhD Research Scholar, you will join an ambitious research community with access to leading organizations, national register data, and advanced AI infrastructure. We invite applications on the following major grand challenges: AI for Business and the Silver Economy. AI is reshaping organizations, strategies, and workforce skills, while demographic aging creates both challenges and opportunities for business innovation and sustainable growth. These shifts call for new insights into strategy, competition, and organizational adaptation.

The center’s research focuses primarily on five key areas:

• Business intelligence
• Consumer Psychology and Technology Adoption
• Creating and capturing sustainable value
• Governance Leadership and Change
• Future of Work
Applications within all these areas are welcome. E-mail: bram.timmermans@nhh.no or lasse.lien@nhh.no

Global Strategy / International Business – with a focus on digital transformation and geopoliticsGlobal Strategy investigates how the global context shapes firms’ strategies and strategic management. Recent geopolitical events, rising populism that weakens global institutions, and the urgency of grand social and environmental challenges are redrawing that context and creating rich research opportunities. In parallel, advances in digital technologies - including AI and Industry 4.0 - challenge core assumptions in International Business, reshaping where firms expand, how they organize cross-border activities, and how they compete. We welcome proposals that explore these themes and their intersections using primarily quantitative methods. We are explicitly open to candidates from adjacent disciplines - such as political science, international relations, or information systems - who seek to integrate their perspectives to advance Global Strategy and International Business research.E-mail: bjorn.schmeisser@nhh.no

Productive Alone but Wiser Together? AI and Collective Knowledge Building in OrganizationsMeeting, learning from, and sharing with colleagues is central to how organizations build collective knowledge. As employees increasingly turn to AI and large language models as sparring partners, these interactions may be quietly displaced. Organizations want to encourage AI use for productivity and efficiency, yet they also need to preserve the organic social interactions through which collective knowledge is built. Early evidence highlights this tension: AI assistance can raise individual performance while narrowing the knowledge groups draw on, and contributions to public knowledge-sharing communities have fallen since generative AI arrived. Far less is known about how this plays out inside organizations. The project will examine what organizations can do, and which work designs can help balance individual productivity with collective knowledge building in the age of AI. We especially welcome candidates interested in Information Systems, Systems Thinking or Organization Theory, and in qualitative research within organizations adopting AI.Email: vidya.oruganti@nhh.no

The Future of Human Resource Management (HRM)Rapid technological change is transforming how we work, organize, and lead. Remote and hybrid work, digital collaboration tools, and AI are creating new opportunities and challenges for organizations and employees. We invite PhD candidates to develop original research on these transformations in a Nordic context, where collaboration among employers, employees, and labor unions plays a central role. As a PhD Research Scholar, you will join an active research environment, work closely with experienced faculty, and contribute new knowledge about how technology is shaping HRM and the future of work.E-mail: karen.olsen@nhh.no

The Board of Directors (BoD) as Strategic Partner and Change AgentThe role of the Board of Directors has evolved from monitoring performance, controlling the financials and approving strategy to becoming increasingly involved in and responsible for the strategic direction of the firm, particularly as a partner to the top management team supporting strategic renewal and innovation in the established firm. Research questions of interest include: exploring the processes through which BoDs initiate and influence strategic change and renewal, the collaborative dynamics between BoDs and senior management, and internal board dynamics.E-mail: inger.stensaker@nhh.no

Teams and cooperationMuch of the value-creating work in organizations takes place in teams, from project and product teams to top management teams and corporate boards. We invite proposals that examine what makes teams work effectively, and how relationships, norms and patterns of interaction within teams form, develop and change over time. Possible areas include, but are not limited to:

• Team start-up and development: How do early interactions and launch processes shape later team dynamics and performance?
• Psychological safety: How does psychological safety emerge, vary and erode over time, and how does it relate to learning, error handling, voice and performance?
• Boards as teams: What characterizes boardroom dynamics? How do interpersonal processes in boards, such as trust, dissent, information sharing and the board–CEO relationship, affect board effectiveness and the quality of governance?
• Humans and AI in teams: What opportunities and challenges emerge when AI is integrated into teamwork? How does it change coordination, roles, trust and learning?
• Emotions in teams: What role do emotions and emotional dynamics play in team processes and performance?
We welcome a range of methodological approaches, including experiments, longitudinal field studies, qualitative research and multi-method designs. Applicants are encouraged to develop their own research questions within this broad area.E-mail: therese.egeland@nhh.no

Consumer trust in AI agentsArtificial intelligence is increasingly taking on roles traditionally performed by humans in marketing, including recommending products, generating advertising content, handling customer service interactions, and personalizing communications. As consumers encounter AI more frequently throughout the customer journey, researchers are seeking to understand how they perceive, evaluate, and respond to AI-based interactions. Key issues include consumer trust; perceived competence and warmth in AI systems; algorithm aversion versus algorithm appreciation; and the conditions under which consumers prefer AI agents over human employees. In this project, the main questions are: What factors facilitate trust in AI agents? Under what conditions do consumers prefer AI agents over human representatives for marketing-related tasks such as product recommendation, customer support, and service recovery?E-mail: magne.supphellen@nhh.no

Export brandingMany exporters in B2C and B2B markets use country-of-origin information in foreign-market communication. Previous research shows that such information can significantly affect brand evaluation and sales of export brands. Origin is often communicated as a simple extrinsic cue, for instance, through a made-in label. However, exporters can achieve greater leverage from origin by including favorable origin elements in export brand positioning. More research is needed on exporters' current practices and how they can leverage origin more effectively: To what extent do exporters include origin information in the brand positioning? When is this more and less effective? How is this practice different in B2B and B2C markets? What procedures do exporters use to integrate origin, and which normative, theory-based procedures can be developed?E-mail: magne.supphellen@nhh.no
The PhD programme
The PhD programme at NHH is a four-year fully-funded programme, which combines an intensive course component and research, preparing the school’s graduates for scholarly positions at reputable research institutions and positions in knowledge-intensive organisations both within and outside academia. Former PhD graduates have been hired by renowned institutions such as Harvard University, The University of Sydney’s Business School, University of Amsterdam, University of St. Gallen, Tilburg University, Stockholm School of Economics, Copenhagen Business School, Hanken School of Economics, Norwegian universities and business schools, as well as by government, banking, finance and consulting industries.

The PhD research scholars will be included in a highly stimulating and rewarding research environment, working closely with faculty members and fellow PhD research scholars. PhD research scholars participate actively in faculty and research seminars, as well as in workshops. As part of the position, the PhD research scholars allocate 25% of their time to career promoting work such as teaching assistance. They also receive pedagogical training. The place of work is at NHH in Bergen, where the PhD research scholars will have their own office space at their department.

The PhD programme gives preference to applicants who address research questions that align with the department’s research interests and the available resources for supervision. As the school aspires gender balance and diversity, female applicants will be given preference if applicants are otherwise equally qualified.

The Department of Strategy and Management requires you to demonstrate both an adequate level of academic skills and an adequate level of English language proficiency (unless you are exempt). We accept the following tests:

• GMAT or GRE tests to measure your academic skills
• TOEFL, IELTS or PTE Academic to measure your English language proficiency
When applying, you are required to upload a copy of your unofficial test scores in Jobbnorge before the deadline. If you are shortlisted, NHH will ask you to give us access to your official test scores without delay.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Behavioral and Experimental Economics
jobs.description:
About the position
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in behavioral and experimental economics at the Department of Economics, as part of the FAIR Markets research project funded by the European Research Council (Project 101267064). The duration of the position is three years.The postdoctoral position offers a unique opportunity to join an ambitious research environment in behavioral and experimental economics and to become an integral part of the FAIR – Centre for Experimental Research on Fairness, Inequality and Rationality and the Department of Economics (FAIR) at the Department of Economics.The successful candidate will join an ambitious new research agenda on the moral foundations of markets and work closely with Bertil Tungodden and other researchers at FAIR and The Choice Lab on projects combining experimental methods, large-scale surveys, and rich administrative data to study how people evaluate the fairness and legitimacy of market transactions. The position provides substantial scope for intellectual contribution and for developing independent research within the broader FAIR Markets agenda.
 
We are looking for a highly ambitious and collaborative researcher with a strong background in behavioral and experimental economics and a particular interest in questions related to fairness, markets, and public policy. The successful candidate should have excellent analytical and technical skills. The ideal candidate will combine methodological rigor with creativity and a strong motivation to contribute to high-quality research aimed at publication in leading international journals.The department seeks ambitious candidates early in their careers. Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD degree in a business-oriented field such as economics or a closely related field from a recognised business school or university.
NHH offers
• Competitive terms depending on the level of competence/length of service.
• An academically stimulating working environment.
• A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
• Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild, coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities – as well as a family-friendly environment (explore visitnorway.com).

The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates.Applicants are requested to present a research statement with their application. The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers, a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal.
