Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  

Universitetet ønsker bedre kjønnsbalanse i stipendiatstillinger innenfor fagområdet og oppfordrer derfor særlig kvinner til å søke. Ved tilnærmet like kvalifikasjoner kan kvinner bli prioritert i samsvar med gjeldende regelverk.

Søk stillingen ved å klikke på "Søk stillingen" på denne siden. 

I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd

• attester og annen dokumentasjon som vurderes relevant for søknaden 
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den engelske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 2.200 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for grønn og bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjente.Det teknisk-naturvitenskapelige fakultet tilbyr utdanninger på bachelor-, master- og doktorgradsnivå. Fakultetet har sterke bånd til både forskningsinstitusjoner og industri. Nesten 40 % av budsjettet er eksternt finansiert. Studentene våre har tett kontakt med næringslivet, og mange master- og doktorgradsoppgaver blir skrevet i samarbeid med industrien. Fakultetet har etablert forskningssamarbeid med universiteter over hele verden, og har flere fagmiljø som er internasjonalt ledende. Fakultetet har om lag 3000 studenter og rundt 500 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen og seks institutt: institutt for data- og elektroteknikk, institutt for maskin, bygg og materialteknologi, institutt for matematikk og fysikk, institutt for kjemi, biovitenskap og miljøteknologi, institutt for energi- og petroleumsteknologi og institutt for sikkerhet, økonomi og planlegging. Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi driver forskning innen datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, elkraft, signalbehandling og medisinsk teknologi. Instituttet er også vert for forskningsnettverket Stavanger AI Lab, og tilbyr bachelor- og masterutdanninger i elektroteknikk, datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, kunstig intelligens og medisinsk teknologi. I tillegg tilbys ph.d.-utdanning i de samme fagområdene.

jobs.occupation: We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer!
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Mechanical Engineer for an assignment with one of our clients within the subsea and energy industry.

 

The position combines mechanical design with technical project responsibility. You will be responsible for engineering activities in projects involving standard and customized products, from design and planning through fabrication, assembly and testing.

 

The assignment is based in Bergen, with office-based work five days per week. Some travel to the client’s production and testing facility should be expected.

 

Responsibilities:

• Lead and coordinate engineering activities in projects involving standard and customized products.
• Design metering systems and related mechanical equipment.
• Take responsibility for the engineering scope throughout project execution.
• Develop and maintain engineering plans and ensure progress against project schedules.
• Coordinate engineering activities and resources in cooperation with the Project Manager.
• Develop 3D CAD models of components and complete systems.
• Prepare fabrication documentation, engineering drawings and procedures.
• Perform internal and external design reviews.
• Review and approve engineering drawings and technical documentation.
• Follow up components, sub-suppliers, fabrication and production activities as required.
• Support assembly and testing activities at the production facility.
• Participate in equipment testing when required.
• Support the Project Manager with engineering expertise and technical input.
• Participate in client meetings where technical expertise is required.
• Ensure designs comply with relevant industry standards, safety requirements, regulations and client specifications.
• Identify opportunities for technical improvements and cost-efficient solutions.
• Coordinate independently with relevant stakeholders, including suppliers, clients, project management and engineering disciplines.
• Ensure high standards of HSE, quality and engineering practice throughout project execution.
 

Qualifications:

• BSc or MSc within Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Design or a related discipline.
• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience within mechanical design and project execution.
• Experience with Creo or an equivalent 3D CAD system is essential.
• Experience with Teamcenter is highly preferred.
• Experience from subsea, oil & gas, offshore or other technically complex industries is preferred.
• Experience with metering and measurement systems is considered an advantage.
• Experience working with mechanical systems, equipment integration, fabrication and testing.
• Experience coordinating engineering activities within projects.
• Good understanding of engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
• Good written and spoken English.
 

Personal skills:

• Proactive and self-driven, with the ability to take ownership of engineering activities from planning through delivery.
• Structured and solution-oriented, with a strong focus on quality and deadlines.
• Confident in making technical decisions based on engineering data, experience and risk assessment.
• Able to balance technical requirements, cost and schedule considerations.
• Strong communication skills and comfortable working with clients, suppliers and multidisciplinary project teams.
• Collaborative and able to coordinate effectively across engineering, project management, production and testing.
• Practical and hands-on in your approach, with an interest in following the product from engineering through assembly and testing.
• Comfortable working independently and taking responsibility for progress within your area.
 

Apply for the position with just a few clicks:Click "Apply Now" and use, for example, your LinkedIn profile for very easy registration. You can also use Vipps, Microsoft, Google, or Facebook.We ask you to upload your CV in Word format, as well as upload your complete transcript.Folk offers:

• Long-term and good opportunities with our clients
• Individual and tailored follow-up during the assignment
• Good career opportunities in various industries
• Competitive conditions
• Social events and pleasant acknowledgments throughout the year
We encourage everyone with relevant experience and/or education to apply, regardless of gender identity, age, origin, or background. At Folk, we are committed to maintaining high employee satisfaction and we offer a dynamic environment with good career opportunities.We see potential in your skills!Folk AS uses a simple and user-friendly candidate system.By keeping your profile updated, you increase the likelihood that we can match your skills to relevant positions.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Since the establishment in 2004, Folk AS has assisted Norwegian and international companies by selecting and recruiting skilled people within technical and administrative disciplines – for project-based, temporary and permanent positions This is what we are good at – here lies our expertise.Our values are: ethical, personal, committed and flexible.

Kandidaten blir en del av gruppen Datasentrert og sikker databehandling (DSComputing), koblet til internasjonale miljøer innen IEEE Blockchain og nettverket for Blockchain Research and Applications (BCRA). Dette miljøet gir en unik mulighet til å kombinere banebrytende blokkjede utforminger og tjenester med relevante anvendelser.

Dette samarbeidsnettverket er bygget på den europeiske blokkjedeinfrastrukturen (EBSI) og sikrer trygg, etterprøvbar datadeling i fullt samsvar med EUs regelverk for kryptoeiendeler (MiCA). 1) Sikker og prosessorientert sammensetning av digitale aktiva og tjenester på tvers av organisasjoner; 2) Sikker og kvalitetssikret tjenesteoppdagelse, integrasjon og automatisering; 3) Pålitelig, adaptiv og kvalitetssikret testing av forretningsapplikasjoner; 4) Automatisk samsvarsvalidering og overvinnelse av barrierer. 

Det foreslåtte økosystemet vil øke konkurranseevnen og kapasiteten for automatisert databehandling i en føderasjon. Integrering og validering av banebrytende teknologier vil gi forbedringer i cybersamarbeid for applikasjoner distribuert i heterogene infrastrukturer. Ved å integrere etiske aspekter i et menneskeorientert design, kan sømløst samarbeid mellom mennesker og databehandlingssystemer realiseres

UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  

Universitetet ønsker bedre kjønnsbalanse i stipendiatstillinger innenfor fagområdet og oppfordrer derfor særlig kvinner til å søke. Ved tilnærmet like kvalifikasjoner kan kvinner bli prioritert i samsvar med gjeldende regelverk.
Slik søker du
Søk stillingen ved å klikke på "Søk stillingen" på denne siden. 

I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

• motivasjonsbrev som beskriver din interesse for prosjektet, herunder fødererte blokkjedeteknologier, og som redegjør for hvordan din faglige bakgrunn, kompetanse og erfaring er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd
• publikasjoner eller annet relevant forskningsarbeid
• attester og annen dokumentasjon som vurderes relevant for søknaden 
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 2.200 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for grønn og bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjente.

Det teknisk-naturvitenskapelige fakultet tilbyr utdanninger på bachelor-, master- og doktorgradsnivå. Fakultetet har sterke bånd til både forskningsinstitusjoner og industri. Nesten 40 % av budsjettet er eksternt finansiert. Studentene våre har tett kontakt med næringslivet, og mange master- og doktorgradsoppgaver blir skrevet i samarbeid med industrien. Fakultetet har etablert forskningssamarbeid med universiteter over hele verden, og har flere fagmiljø som er internasjonalt ledende. Fakultetet har om lag 3000 studenter og rundt 500 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen og seks institutt: institutt for data- og elektroteknikk, institutt for maskin, bygg og materialteknologi, institutt for matematikk og fysikk, institutt for kjemi, biovitenskap og miljøteknologi, institutt for energi- og petroleumsteknologi og institutt for sikkerhet, økonomi og planlegging. Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi driver forskning innen datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, elkraft, signalbehandling og medisinsk teknologi. Instituttet er også vert for forskningsnettverket Stavanger AI Lab, og tilbyr bachelor- og masterutdanninger i elektroteknikk, datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, kunstig intelligens og medisinsk teknologi. I tillegg tilbys ph.d.-utdanning i de samme fagområdene.

jobs.occupation: Field Application Engineer
jobs.description:
At Six Robotics, we build intelligent software that gives Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) the ability to collaborate, adapt on the fly, and execute missions that were previously impossible. From our base in Oslo, our 70+ experts in defence, software, and AI develop our flagship autonomy and swarm platform used by both government and industry. In close partnership with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), we move fast from concept to live deployment, often in the field alongside end users.

We work with advanced hardware and software, a modern tech stack, and missions that demand both technical mastery and operational discipline. Everyone is close to the action, from deep technical problem-solving to field operations. We move fast and value clarity, integrity, and teamwork in everything we do.

At Six Robotics, every person executes with precision, adapts to changing conditions, and strengthens the team. We only hire the best. Getting in is hard, and you’ll be challenged every day. But if you have the skill, the discipline, and the drive to push your limits, you’ll find no better place to deliver real-world impact while collaborating and learning from the best in the field.

About the role
We’re scaling fast, and to meet growing demand from both customers and internal teams, we’re expanding our Field Application Engineering team. Today, we are seven engineers split into two focused units: one driving internal testing and system validation, the other leading customer-facing work like demos, onboarding, and training. Together, this team is responsible for one thing above all else: making sure our technical works where it actually matters.

As a Field Application Engineer at Six Robotics, you sit at the intersection of product, engineering, and operators. You’ll take cutting-edge autonomy software out into the field, where constraints are real, stakes are high, and feedback is immediate. What you learn in the field directly shapes what we build next.

The role requires extensive travel (approximately 150 days per year), both nationally and internationally. This is not a desk role. You will spend most of your time in the field, working side-by-side with operators, testing systems under real conditions, troubleshooting when things don’t go as planned, and making sure every deployment delivers real operational value.

What you will do
• 
Own customer integrations: take part in technical pre-sales, lead onboarding, capture requirements, and ensure our swarm software is seamlessly integrated and fully operational.

• 
Turn needs into plans: create integration steps, checklists, and test procedures that guide both customers and our teams.

• 
Run field tests: plan and execute acceptance tests and trials, analyze telemetry, and feed results back into product and engineering.

• 
Troubleshoot issues: diagnose and resolve problems across hardware, firmware, networking, and software, often in time-critical situations.

• 
Deliver customer demos: plan and execute high-quality demos that communicate the value of our technology to customers and partners.

• 
Train and onboarding users: ensure operators understand how to use our systems effectively through structured training and hands-on support.

• 
Document and scale: build playbooks, runbooks, and internal best practices to support customers and future field engineers.

• 
Be the technical face in the field: act as the bridge between customers, operators, and internal teams, ensuring alignment and continuous improvement.

What we are looking for
We’re looking for a Field Application Engineer who is as comfortable in front of people as they are working hands-on with complex systems in the field. You are outgoing, robust, and adaptable, someone who thrives in dynamic environments where plans change and challenges arise. You bring structure to complexity, communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and take ownership from problem to solution.

You’re a creative problem solver who isn’t afraid to get your hands dirty, whether that means debugging systems in the field, setting up hardware, or working through unexpected issues under pressure. At the same time, you are confident in explaining complex concepts, building customer trust, and representing Six Robotics externally.

To be a strong fit for the role, we believe you:

• 
Have a strong technical foundation: ability to set up, configure, and troubleshoot complex systems across networking, hardware, and software.

• 
Are structured and reliable: capable of managing multiple workstreams, stakeholders, and field activities without losing clarity or momentum.

• 
Is an excellent communicator: able to explain complex technical concepts to operators, customers, and internal teams.

• 
Are hands-on and proactive: you take initiative, solve problems end-to-end, and are comfortable working directly with hardware and systems in the field.

• 
Are willing to travel extensively: able and motivated to spend around 150 days per year in the field, both nationally and internationally.

• 
Are fluent in English; Norwegian is a strong advantage. German or French is a plus.

In addition to the above, experience with UAVs, robotics, defence, or similar complex systems would be valuable. Familiarity with military organizations or prior field-based, customer-facing technical work is a plus. Basic programming skills or the ability to read code would also be beneficial.

Why you should join
At Six Robotics, we build systems that work when it matters the most. If you're driven by meaningful problems, technical depth, and the chance to shape something from the ground up, you'll find your place here.

• 
Contribute to a mission with urgency: Help build autonomy that protects nations and deters conflict in an era defined by unmanned warfare. The problems are real, the stakes are high, and the need is now.

• 
Take ownership from day one: You’ll be trusted with real responsibility early, with the autonomy to move fast and solve hard problems without unnecessary layers.

• 
Build from zero, shape the future: Join early and help shape the systems, tools, and ways of working as we scale. What you build is used in real operations, with a short and clear feedback loop between your work and its impact.

• 
Work with purpose, supported by great benefits: Be part of a team of smart, driven, and engaged individuals who take pride in their work and push each other to improve. We offer competitive compensation, equity potential, and solid insurance and pension plans.

Our recruitment process
We aim to keep our process short and sweet, but also thorough. As a small team, every hire matters, and we can’t afford to get this one wrong.

Here’s what to expect:

• 
Screening interview with one of our recruiters to get to know you better (30 min).

• 
Meet & Greet with someone from the team to get to know each other better (60 min).

• 
Structured case interview to understand role fit and potential (90 min).

• 
Final interview with Head of People to assess cultural fit (45 min).

• 
Reference check followed by an offer if everything goes well.

We will review applications on an ongoing basis.

All employees at Six Robotics are required to undergo a security clearance (Sikkerhetsklarering) due to our close collaboration with the Norwegian Armed Forces. Prior clearance is not required; the process begins as part of onboarding. As part of this process, eligibility is limited to candidates holding citizenship from EU and NATO member countries.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
We exist to strengthen defence, protect nations, and deter conflict in an era defined by unmanned warfare. Our mission is to multiply operational capabilities, accelerate the transition to robotic warfare, and give NATO and our allies a decisive advantage in the new era of unmanned operations.

We overcome the limits of current systems with collaborative swarm autonomy, enabling unmanned systems to act as one. Our software lets drones collaborate, adapt, and execute missions as a team, allowing a single operator to control an army of robots, accelerate decisions, and multiply combat effectiveness.

jobs.occupation: Researcher
jobs.description:
About the Role
The Norwegian Meteorological Institute has an open position as Researcher. The position is affiliated with the Ocean and Ice Division in the Ocean Department, and is based in Tromsø. The Ocean and Ice Division develops and operates numerical models for forecasting of ocean currents, hydrography, sea level, waves and sea-ice. These models provide input to downstream services such as oil spill drift models and search-and-rescue support. The work is carried out in collaboration with national and international partners.

The work involves the management of operational forecast systems, including coordination of research staff, project administration, and supervision of research activities. The candidate is expected to contribute in the development of the division's research portfolio according to the institute strategy and actively seeks external project funding. Furthermore, the successful candidate will be expected to coordinate and manage inter-institutional activities that MET Norway is partnering in. It is essential that you can work efficiently in a team environment both within MET Norway and in an inter-institutional framework.
 
Among the tasks that the successful candidate will become involved in, is management of MET Norway's responsibilities in the Arctic Monitoring and Forecasting Centre (ARCMFC) of the Copernicus Marine Service. ARCMFC is coordinated by the Nansen Environmental and Remote Sensing Center, and also includes the Institute of Marine Research, Norway and the Danish Meteorological Institute. Met Norway's main responsibilities in ARCMFC are wave modelling, near real time forecasts for ocean circulation and sea ice, management and monitoring of communications with the service central dissemination unit at Copernicus, and monitoring of product quality.

The successful candidate will act as a link between the Ocean and Ice Division, the Fram Centre in Tromsø, and ARCMFC and become involved in regional high resolution ocean and sea ice modelling for our national service, notably the application of ARCMFC results for this service. Probabilistic forecasting is of particular interest in this context. 
Qualifications
• PhD in geophysical/physical sciences, with emphasis on remote sensing techniques and/or physical oceanography.
• Minimum 10 years of experience after PhD as an independent scientist with a strong record of peer-review publications. International experience is a requirement
• Experience with management and/or technical implementations of operational forecast systems in either operational oceanography or weather prediction is expected
• Strong track record with success in obtaining competitive research funding is beneficial (e.g. Research Council of Norway, EU Horizon  ESA )
• Experience in scientific programming within a Linux environment (Fortran, Python, Git)
• Experience with numerical ocean and/or sea-ice models.
• The working language at MET Norway is Norwegian. Foreign candidates must be willing to learn basic Norwegian.
• Candidates must be able to work effectively in English and demonstrate fluency, written and oralWe offer
• Salary: NOK 840.000 - 940.000 per year, depending on qualifications and experience. For particularly qualified candidates, a higher salary may be considered. A 2% statutory contribution to SPK is deducted from the salary
• Membership in The Norwegian Service Pension fund (SPK) which offers great pension, insurance and mortgage terms(read more here: https://spk.no/en/membership-in-spk/)
• Flexible working hours
• Employees may use up to one hour of working time per week for physical exerces 
• There is a six months mutual probitionary period 
• work place in TromsøDiversity and positive action
We emphasize diversity and therefore encourage everyone qualified to apply for a job regardless of age, gender, disability, national or ethnic background. MET practice positive action, and will call at least one qualified applicant in each of these groups for an interview: applicants with a disability, immigrant background or gaps in the CV. To be considered in one or more of these categories, you must mark the appropriate category in your application.

The ticks can be used for anonymised statistics or reporting purposes.

Publication of applicant lists for public sector positions is an important principle to ensure transparency. If you want your name to be excluded from the applicant list, you must ask for it yourself, and give us a reason. In order to be exempted from the public applicant list, your justification for exemption must outweigh the consideration of transparency in the applicant list. If your request is not accepted, you will have the opportunity to withdraw your application.
The application
The application with CV and other attachments is sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. Attach certificates and all pages of diplomas. The documents must be in Norwegian, a Scandinavian language or English. Translations must be authorized. Before any employment, we will check the documents. In the case of foreign education, we ask that you attach an explanation of the grading system.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Modern meteorology requires management and analysis of enormous amounts of data, and offers great and exciting professional challenges. Since the institute was established in 1866, the Norwegian meteorologists have played a key role in this development. 

Norwegian Meteorological Institute is today a leading international environment of expertise in operational meteorology and climatology.

jobs.occupation: Senior Engineer
jobs.description:
About the position
A permanent position as Senior engineer (position code 1181) is available at The Department of Physics, University of Oslo.

Starting date as soon as possible. 

Place of work is Department of Physics at Blindern, Oslo.
Job description and work tasks
The Electronics section has seven academic positions (two full-time and five part-time) and two technical positions. The research activity is currently largely related to projects in medical technology, particularly those using methods based on impedance spectroscopy. The successful candidate may also provide technical support for new research activities in electronic components and neuromorphic electronics, especially related to electrical characterization, measurement setups, and laboratory infrastructure. 

Together with the Department of Informatics, the section is responsible for a study program in electronics, informatics, and technology. The academic staff are therefore responsible for several courses in electronics and sensor technology and also contribute to teaching basic physics courses. The section’s staff are also involved in the supervision of students at both master’s and doctoral level. 

The engineering position is intended to support both the research and teaching activities in which the section is involved. 

The tasks connected to teaching will primarily involve training and assisting master’s and PhD students in the use of specialized measuring instruments and software. 

Part of the position also involves organizing the section’s student laboratories. This includes testing of hardware and software, as well as other typical engineering tasks related to the day to-day operation of the laboratories.
What skills are important in this role?
Qualification requirements:

The minimum educational requirement is a master’s degree (or equivalent) in electronics/electrical engineering. In addition, the candidate must have experience with: 

• Instrumentation, measurement systems, and laboratory work 
• Impedance spectroscopy and interpretation of bioimpedance data 
• Programming in Python and MATLAB, or equivalent 
• Finite element modelling, e.g. COMSOL Multiphysics 
• Good oral and written English skills
The following qualifications are strongly desirable and will be emphasized in the evaluation process: 

• Research experience, preferably demonstrated through a PhD degree 
• Use of various sensors for monitoring food quality, such as colorimetry, pH measurements, and NIR spectrometry 
• Electrical characterization of semiconductor devices or other electronic components, preferably including low-current and/or pulsed measurements 
• Automation and integration of laboratory instruments and measurement systems 
• Technical supervision of studentsWhat are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• A service minded attitude 
• Ability to work independently 
• Ability to work precisely in a structured and solution-oriented manner and swiftly adapts to new tasks 
• Good communication and collaboration skills 
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods 
• Have a safety-oriented attitude
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal skills.
We can offer you
• A pleasant and stimulating work environment
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
• Salary in position as Senior Engineer, position code 1181 in salary range NOK 700 000 – 775 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2% is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension FundWe need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We especially encourage women to apply.We hope you will apply for the position with us.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter with a statement of motivation
• CV (complete overview of education and work experience)
• Copies of educational certificates and transcript of records
• Names and contact details of 2-3 references (names, relation to candidate and telephone number)
Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
Formal regulations
The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The research at the Department of Physics covers a broad range of subfields within physics and technology: From space research to medical physics. A good proportion of the research is interdisciplinary, and conducted in close cooperation with collaborators in Norway and abroad. Education and teaching are other essential activities. We offer a broad range of courses, and the Department is involved in several study programmes at bachelor’s and master’s level. Some of the best lecturers in Norway are amongst our employees, and we are proud of our prizewinning teaching and learning environment. The Department has 200 employees, of which 50 are permanent scientific positions. On a yearly basis 20 students complete their Ph.D. and 50 finish their M.Sc. degree.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Integrative Global Change Biology
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you a motivated researcher who wants to take a step towards a doctorate degree? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will join a vibrant evolutionary ecology group, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
We are looking for a PhD candidate to be part of an interdisciplinary team investigating geographic variation in how European insects cope with the combined stress of higher temperatures and drier conditions. There is growing evidence that insect populations are declining around the world, making the proposed research timely and important.

This project builds on research comparing the physiological responses of insect species from contrasting climates to better understand future responses to changes in temperature and precipitation. The PhD position will be focused primarily on understanding the plastic and evolved responses of insects to temperature and hydric stress. The expected research will include a combination of field and lab work, including insect husbandry, and physiological experiments characterizing thermal and desiccation tolerance. The position will require statistical analyses and potentially the development of eco-evolutionary biophysical models. The results of this work are expected to be disseminated in the scientific literature as well as to the public and relevant stakeholders. The primary supervisor for this position will be Professor Cameron Ghalambor. 
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the Biodiversity, Ecology, and Evolution research group as part of the Ghalambor lab 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching experience in courses related to Ecology and Evolution
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD programme in Biology, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in biology or equivalent with relevant background in evolutionary biology, ecology, entomology, physiology, or similar. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than December 2026.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You have excellent written and oral English language skills 
• You have some experience conducting statistical analyses using R or other statistical languages.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• You have experience conducting field and lab research with insects, or a willingness to learn 
• You have the ability to collect data in rigorous, repeatable, and transparent way
• You have good data management skills
• You have demonstrated strong quantitative & analytical skills
• You can code in R, Python, and or other statistical languages
• You can demonstrate strong scientific writing skills
• You can demonstrate the ability to complete tasks in a timely manner
• You work well in a collaborative environmentPersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Be passionate about pursuing knowledge and scholarship in your field
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Have a strong motivation to read and be familiar with the primary literature
• Be able to interpret results and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
• Communicate effectively in writing, speaking, and public presentations 
• Work well as part of a team with diverse research interests
• Be self-motivated and enthusiastic about your research topic and for dissemination of scientific research, both through journal articles and public engagement
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU

jobs.description:
About the positions
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applications for two postdoctoral positions in applied microeconomics at the Department of Economics. The duration of each position is three years.The postdoctoral positions offer a unique opportunity to join an ambitious research environment in applied microeconomics and to become an integral part of the FAIR- Centre for Experimental Research on Fairness, Inequality and Rationality and the Department Economics (FAIR) at the Department of Economics. The successful candidates will work closely with researchers at FAIR on one of two research projects:Postdoctoral Position 1: FOUNDATIONS: The Foundations of Labor ProductivityThe FOUNDATIONS project is funded by the European Research Council (Project 101302557). The successful candidate will work closely with Alexander Willén and other researchers on projects examining how labor-market structures shape worker sorting and learning, firm strategy, workplace organisation, and productivity. The research combines large-scale surveys and experiments with population-wide administrative data and detailed firm-level information, with a particular focus on questions related to market power, human capital, and productivity.

Postdoctoral Position 2: Labor-Market Structures, Working Conditions, and Worker Well-BeingThis project is funded by NFR Fripro grant 360300. The successful candidate will work closely with Katrine Løken and Alexander Willén, and other researchers at FAIR on projects examining how labor-market structures and institutions shape working conditions and workers’ broader life outcomes. The research will combine rich administrative data, linked survey data, and empirical methods to study questions related to employer power, worker voice and unions, workplace environment, and worker well-being.

Both positions provide substantial scope for intellectual contribution and for developing independent research within the respective research agendas.We are looking for highly ambitious and collaborative researchers with a strong background in applied microeconomics, particularly labor, public, personnel, or organisational economics. The ideal candidates will have excellent empirical, analytical, and technical skills and combine methodological rigor with creativity and a strong motivation to produce research aimed at publication in leading international journals.The department seeks ambitious candidates early in their careers. About the position
Do you want to work as a researcher in the field of host-microbiome interactions in human liver disease funded by the ERC?

One position is available as Researcher (SKO1109) - a temporary 3-year position - at Research Institute of Internal Medicine at Institute of Clinical Medicine, funded by an ERC/ European Research Council Consolidator grant.

Research Institute of Internal Medicine at the Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo, is physically located at Rikshospitalet, Oslo University Hospital, and consists of 6 research groups, and a total of about 60 employees. The research profile of the Institute is to combine clinical medicine and molecular biology to establish a bridge between bench and bedside. This is of utmost importance to exploit in clinical medicine the recent development in immunology, biochemistry and molecular biology with the ambitious aim of developing novel treatment modalities and new diagnostic tools.

Integrated in the institute is the Norwegian PSC Research Center (NoPSC), which is a world-leading center dedicated to research on the chronic liver disease primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Several features make PSC an intriguing model disease; more than 80% of the patients have inflammatory bowel disease, for which the link with the biliary inflammation is poorly known, and the disease may recur after liver transplantation. The center comprises three research groups covering all aspects of research related to primary sclerosing cholangitis, from basic genomic and experimental studies to clinical research and clinical trials.
More about the position
The research group, led by Prof. Johannes Hov, has over the last decade established a strong clinical and translational microbiome research environment with access to a wide range of tools including metagenomics, mouse models and a germ-free animal facility. The group has recently successfully completed the ERC Starting Grant project “StopAutoimmunity”, which has led to several important discoveries.

We are now seeking a skilled and ambitious co-worker to take on challenging projects in the context of the European Research Council (ERC) Consolidator Grant “FatVersusBile”, which focuses on how the gut drives liver health in humans and mice, in particular, in the setting of inflammatory bowel disease. jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Experimental Proton Therapy
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a three-year PhD Research Fellow position in experimental proton therapy, available at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo (UiO).

The preferred starting date is March 1, 2027, and no later than April 1, 2027.The fellowship period is 36 months.

The position is part of InnovaRTBRAIN – Innovative Radiation Therapy for Brain Tumors, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) funded by the European Union. The network brings together leading European research institutions, hospitals, and industrial partners to develop innovative radiation therapy approaches for brain tumors, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma.The successful candidate will be recruited as Doctoral Candidate 13 (DC13) and will join the proton therapy research group at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo and the Department of Radiation Biology, Oslo University Hospital (OUS).

Most of the experimental research will be carried out at the proton therapy facility at Oslo University Hospital, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for preclinical proton irradiation, including a dedicated research beamline and gantry, a 3T small-animal MRI scanner, and facilities for experimental radiobiology.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo. 
Background of the project
Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive forms of brain cancer, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Radiation therapy plays a central role in its treatment, but its effectiveness is restricted by tumor radioresistance and the sensitivity of surrounding healthy brain tissue.

Proton minibeam radiation therapy (pMBRT) is an emerging approach in which radiation is delivered in narrow, spatially separated beams, producing a highly heterogeneous dose distribution. This technique has the potential to reduce radiation-induced damage to healthy tissues while maintaining effective tumor irradiation. However, its biological effects, particularly the evolution of tumor and normal tissue responses over time, remain incompletely understood. 
 
The PhD project will investigate the biological response to proton minibeam irradiation in preclinical models of brain cancer, using longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and quantitative image analysis. The project will also explore the potential of MRI-derived biomarkers for assessing treatment response and normal tissue effects. An important part of the research will be conducted in close collaboration with another doctoral candidate in InnovaRTBRAIN (DC6), based at Oslo University Hospital, who will investigate combinations of radiation therapy and immunotherapy, including CAR-T cell treatment.
Job description 
The doctoral candidate will conduct experimental studies in mouse models to investigate tumor and normal tissue responses to proton minibeam radiation therapy, using magnetic resonance imaging and other methods to characterize radiation-induced biological effects.The main responsibilities will be:

• Plan and conduct preclinical proton minibeam irradiation experiments in mouse models
• Acquire and analyze MRI data, including diffusion-weighted imaging, to quantify treatment response and potential normal tissue toxicity
• Relate MR-derived image parameters to radiation dose distributions, linear energy transfer (LET), and biological endpoints
• Develop and apply quantitative image analysis and radiomics methods to identify imaging features associated with tumor response and radiation injury
• Investigate MRI-based biomarkers in combination with NMR-derived metabolic and relaxation-time markers, in collaboration with international project partners
• Collaborate with DC6 on preclinical studies combining proton minibeam radiation therapy and immunotherapy
• Participate in joint research, training activities, and research visits within the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network Research environment
The candidate will join an interdisciplinary research environment combining radiobiology, medical physics, experimental proton therapy, and medical imaging. The research will be conducted in close collaboration between the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital, primarily at the proton therapy research facility at the Norwegian Radium Hospital. The facility provides access to experimental proton irradiation, a dedicated small-animal MRI scanner, treatment planning software, and infrastructure for preclinical cancer research.
Supervisors and international collaboration
The doctoral candidate will be supervised by Professor Eirik Malinen (UiO/OUS), with co-supervision from Professor Nina Edin (UiO), Professor Paul Vasos (University of Bucharest), and Else Marit Inderberg (OUS). The InnovaRTBRAIN network will provide an international and interdisciplinary training environment, combining expertise in medical physics, radiobiology, imaging, cancer biology, and immunotherapy.
Planned secondments
As part of the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network, the candidate will undertake research visits to international academic and industrial partners:

• University of Bucharest, Romania (3 months): Integration of NMR-based biomarkers with MRI-derived radiomics to characterize tumor responses.
• Xstrahl, UK (2 weeks): Training in small-animal irradiation technologies and their applications in preclinical radiation therapy research.
• COSYLAB, Slovenia (2 weeks): Exposure to industrial developments in radiation therapy technology and control systems.
These secondments will provide complementary scientific and technical training and strengthen collaboration within the InnovaRTBRAIN network.

The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Multimodal Sensor Data Fusion for Cultural Heritage
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network GLASS-CARE, collaborate with academic, museums, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on cultural heritage science.

As part of the GLASS-CARE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027, and the Head of the unit will be the immediate supervisor for employment-related matters.
About the project
About the GLASS-CARE project GLASS-CARE (Green Light for Advanced Solutions in Stained-glass Conservation and Application of Research and Education) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, GLASS-CARE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation. For more details, visit http://www.glasscare.eu/

About the DC projectWithin the GLASS-CARE project, the individual research project associated with this position (DC13) is entitled Multi-sensor data fusion for digital representation.

The PhD project will investigate computational approaches for integrating data acquired through hyperspectral imaging (HSI), multispectral imaging (MSI), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), and photoacoustic techniques.

The resulting computational framework will contribute to improved material characterization, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making for historical stained glass.The PhD candidate will address the following objectives (1) Multimodal data integration (2) Multimodal registration, alignment and data fusion (3) Feature extraction and dimensionality reduction (4) Unified digital representations (6) Validation through case studies.

Expected results: (1)  A computational framework for integrating heterogeneous imaging and analytical data into unified digital representations of stained glass. (2) Advanced data fusion methods to minimize redundancy, preserve complementary information, and reveal hidden patterns across different imaging modalities. (3) Deliver validated computational models and tools for improved material characterization, visualisation, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making. 
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Colourlab research group.
• Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person pacross the GLASS-CARE partner institutions and contribute to GLASS-CARE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to project partners in University of Antwerpen-UA Belgium, Nova University Lisbon – UNL Portugal, and Swiss National Museum-SNM Switzerland.
• Other career-promoting work
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have experience with image acquisition and analysis.
• Excellent programming skills.
• At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, imaging science, conservation science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position. 
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
• You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge of and experience with spectral imaging. 
• Knowledge of and experience with data fusion.
• Knowledge of and experience in conservation science will be an added advantage. 
• Experience working in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.
• Programming skills in Python/Matlab.
• Excellent analytical and communication skills.
• Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Have a high level of personal responsibility, initiative, motivation and ability to work in a project team as well as independently. 
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them.
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals.
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback.
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions.
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
 

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
The position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance. In addition, mobility allowance and family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees.
• CV.
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of  completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position. Those who are currently doing their master thesis, submit the summary (3-4 pages).
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1600 words/4 pages).
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page).
• Scientific publications or other documentation of previous research work.
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees.
• Completed GLASS-CARE questionnaire (available at Glass-Care website).
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Evaluation processApplications will be assessed by an expert committee based on the qualifications and documentation submitted by the applicants. The evaluation will consider academic achievements, the quality and relevance of the applicant's educational background, research potential, and suitability for the position. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview. The final appointment will be made in accordance with the applicable regulations for employment at the university.
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Sony George, +47 92556485, email sony.george@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR at the department: hr@idi.ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 31.01.2027

For practical information about working at NTNU, please visit this webpage.
