jobs.occupation: Professor/Associate Professor in Educational Psychology
jobs.description:
About the position
The Department of Education at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position in Educational Psychology. We seek applicants with a strong research interest in counselling practices targeting schools, Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) settings, and/or Educational Psychological Counselling settings. 

Educational systems in Norway and internationally face growing challenges concerning inclusion, diversity, and equity. Addressing these challenges requires stronger collaboration across the education system, including early childhood education and care (ECEC), schools, and support services. It also calls for closer links between research and practice, to improve educational quality and learning outcomes. We are seeking applicants with a research portfolio in these areas. 

The position is suited for candidates who wish to advance research on counselling, implementation processes, and/or organizational development. We particularly encourage applicants whose research focuses on inclusion in educational communities. Relevant experience includes experimental interventions and longitudinal studies involving families or educational settings and examining the conditions that support learning, development, well-being, and engagement. 

We welcome diverse scholarly profiles but particularly value innovative, methodologically rigorous research. Expertise in quantitative methods will be emphasised, while experience integrating qualitative approaches, such as observation of collaboration and interaction, is an advantage. Experience leading large-scale projects, managing complex project structures or coordinating interdisciplinary teams will be valued.

The position involves 47 % teaching, 47 % research, and 6 % administrative tasks.
More about the position
The successful candidate is expected to strengthen research in educational psychology and contribute to the Faculty of Educational Sciences’ research group, Development, Equity and Literacy in Learning Contexts (DEAL). 

The successful candidate is also expected to actively participate in the collective development of our education programs and teach at the bachelor- and master-level programs in Educational Psychology.

The candidates’ scientific production in the past 5 years will be emphasized in the assessment. It is expected that the successful candidate publishes internationally and seeks external funding. 
Work tasks and responsibilities
The appointee must be able to lead and initiate research, supervise doctoral degree students, participate in teaching and examination work at all levels, and undertake administrative tasks, in accordance with applicable provisions. 

More specifically the appointee must:

• Contribute to the development of research and study programs in Educational Psychology
• Contribute to the research group DEAL 
• Participate in national and international research networks 
• Plan, teach, and supervise in the bachelor and master level courses in Educational Psychology 
• Disseminate research 
• Apply for external funding 
• Conduct administrative tasks Qualifications
For Associate Professor:

In this role you must have:

• Doctoral degree within Education Psychology or competence at an equivalent level documented through scientific work of the same scope and quality 
• Documented basic university pedagogical competence. Applicants who do not have documented basic university pedagogical competence must acquire this within two years from appointment
• Good communication skills both written and oral in English and Norwegian or another Scandinavian language at level B2 are a prerequisite for performing all the tasks associated with the position. Applicants who do not master a Scandinavian language at the time of appointment are given a deadline of three years to learn Norwegian
• Publications in high ranked international journals within educational psychology
It is an advantage if you have:

• strong competence and experience in research methods and experience with quantitative methodology related to longitudinal and/or experimental designs 
• experience in obtaining external funds
• experience in leading large-scale research projects
• documentation of qualifications in the field of academic management and administration
For Professor:

In this role you must have:

• Doctoral degree or competence at an equivalent level and a track record that documents efforts and results over time within the field of Educational Psychology.
• Substantial academic production and significant contributions to research at the highest level, in accordance with international or national standards within the field. 
• Success in obtaining grants for major research applications and experience in leading and completing research projects. The research should be of high quality, demonstrating both breadth and depth within the research field and showing the ability to address new issues.
• Research production should reflect an independent research profile, but also the ability to initiate and conduct high-level research in collaboration with other researchers and research institutions. 
• Strong competence and experience in research methods. Experience with quantitative methodology related to longitudinal and/or experimental designs is an advantage.
• Documented basic university pedagogical competence 
• Broad experience in the development and implementation of teaching, supervision and collegial work with high pedagogical quality, as well as a willingness and ability for continuous professional development as a teacher and supervisor.
• Good qualifications in the field of academic leadership and experience with management of research projects or research groups.
• Good communication skills both written and oral in English and Norwegian or another Scandinavian language at level B2 are a prerequisite for performing all the tasks associated with the position. Applicants who do not master a Scandinavian language at the time of appointment are given a deadline of three years to learn Norwegian
• Publications in high ranked international journals within educational psychology.
It is an advantage if you have:

• strong competence and experience in research methods and experience with quantitative methodology related to longitudinal and/or experimental designs
• experience in obtaining external funds
• experience in leading large-scale research projects
• documentation of qualifications in the field of academic management and administrationPersonal skills
• Good/excellent collaborative and communication skills
• Ability to build strong academic environments and promote collaboration and quality
• High work capacity and strong ability to deliver results
• Strong teaching and coaching abilities and experiences
Personal suitability and motivation will be given decisive weight in the assessment.
We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us.
We offer
• Exciting and meaningful responsibilities in an institution with a strong societal mission, contributing to research, education and knowledge dissemination that support sustainable and equitable societal development
• Committed colleagues in an ambitious and collaborative working environment
• Membership in SPK - The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which is one of Norway’s best pension schemes
• Good employee benefits 
• Salary in position as Professor, position code 1013, in a salary range from kr. 865 000 to kr. 1 010 000 depending on competencies. 2 percent of the salary is deducted in statutory contributions to The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Salary in position as Associate Professor, position code 1011, in a salary range from kr. 750 000 to kr. 865 000 depending on competencies. 2 percent of the salary is deducted in statutory contributions to The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund The application must include
• Application letter 
• CV 
• A complete list of publications
• Transcripts, diplomas and certificates
• Educational portfolio of 3-6 pages, providing a comprehensive and systematic presentation of the applicant’s educational expertise. Documenting educational competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own practice and learning vision is anchored in the SoTL criteria (focus on student learning, development over time, a research approach and collegial attitude and practice. For guidance, see this page 
• Documentation and reflection relating to the applicant’s own qualification within the areas of applied knowledge, academic management, administration and personal qualities relevant to the position
• A separate note (one page) where the applicant explains their future plans for research in educational psychology. The note must include ambitions for feasible future research funding and how this can be done in collaboration with other members of the research group DEAL. The content of this note will be given great importance in the process of evaluating and ranking applicants
• Applicants for position as Associate Professor are requested to submit up to 10 academic works with an overview and brief account of their scientific significance and, in case of co-authorship, a description of the applicants' contribution to each publication
• Applicants for position as Professor are requested to submit up to 15 academic works with an overview and brief account of their scientific significance and, in case of co-authorship, a description of the applicants' contribution to each publication
• References (list of 2-3 persons with name, title, email and phone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our online recruitment system Jobbnorge. 

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documents must be in English (or a Scandinavian language).

Incomplete applications will not be assessed. 

Interviews and trial lecture will form part of the appointment process. The entire breadth of qualifications will be assessed in ranking competent applicants.
General information
Please refer to the Rules for employment and promotion for professor and associate Professor positions at the University of Oslo, the Guide for applicants for Professor and Associate professor positions and Rules for practicing the requirement for basic pedagogical competence at the University of Oslo.

Please also see Guidance memo concerning employment and promotion of professors at the Faculty of Educational Sciences, UiO. 

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with the Norwegian Freedom of Information Act §25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You need to justify an exemption, and we will decide whether your request is granted. If we can’t, you will hear from us. 

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees that is intended to secure the rights to all research results etc.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 27 400 students and 6 900 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.The Department of Education  was established in 1938 and is one of three departments at the Faculty of Educational Sciences. Research at the department is characterized by interdisciplinarity and encompasses a broad range of human learning across the entire life course, from early childhood education and care to higher education and workplace learning.The breadth of our research is reflected in our bachelor’s and master’s programmes, which also include an international master’s programme. IPED currently has approximately 90 staff members, comprising around 40 academic full-time equivalents, 30 doctoral research fellows and 20 administrative full-time equivalents. The department has about 700 students.

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellow in Evolutionary Biochemistry
jobs.employer_name: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
jobs.description:
The position
A 4-year PhD position in Evolutionary Biochemistry is available at the Department of Medical Biology, Faculty of Health Sciences, within the Host–Microbe Interaction (HMI) research group. The position is part of the LacZymes project, led by Dr. Christopher Frøhlich.

General information about the position.

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD programme is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25 % each year and will consist of teaching and other duties. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to the PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The project 
Do you hold a Master’s degree in molecular biology (or a related field) and have a strong interest in the molecular mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance development? Are you motivated to conduct interdisciplinary research at one of the northernmost universities in the world? If so, this PhD position may be of interest to you.

The successful candidate will join a project aiming to uncover the molecular mechanisms of AMR evolution at the enzymatic level. To address this, the project integrates ancestral sequence reconstruction, directed evolution, pre-steady-state and steady-state enzyme kinetics, and X-ray crystallography. Candidates with experience in one or more of these areas are encouraged to apply.

The PhD candidate will report to Dr. Christopher Frøhlich and is expected to contribute actively to the project while developing expertise at the interface of molecular biology, enzymology, and evolutionary biology.

The PhD candidate will work on the following tasks: 

• Manage their own research project
• Experimental design and execution
• Enzyme evolution and selection
• Enzyme production and purification
• Biochemical enzyme characterization
• Structural and functional characterization
• Writing scientific papers and a PhD thesis
• Presenting the work in national and international arenas 
Personal characteristics:The applicant should be motivated, creative and ambitious, with a strong ability to work problem-solution orientated both in teams and independently. The applicant should be genuinely interested in the field of molecular evolution and AMR as well as scientific dissemination. In the evaluation of which applicant is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience, and personal suitability, in terms of the qualification requirements specified in this position announcement. The appointment is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants and national guidelines for appointment as PhD fellow

Applicants are required to submit a motivation letter describing how the position aligns with their research interests.
Contact
For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Christopher Frøhlich:

• phone: +47 46 96 87 78
• email: christopher.frohlich@uit.noQualifications
Required qualifications

• Master’s degree in molecular biology, microbiology, chemistry or equivalent education, with a grade of C or better. Candidates who have not yet completed their Master’s education must submit a written statement from their main supervisor stating the tentative date of their Master’s defence.
• Experience in at least two of the following areas: molecular cloning, protein expression and purification, biochemical characterization of enzymes (e.g. kinetic investigations), X-ray crystallography
• Documented oral and written English skills
Applicants must document fluency of in English and be able to work in an international environment. Nordic applicants can document their English capabilities by attaching their high school diploma.  Working knowledge of Norwegian or a Scandinavian language is also beneficial.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience in the field of AMR and AMR mechanisms
• Experience in coding (e.g. Python) and competence with computer-based analytical tools (e.g., Pymol)
• Knowledge of a Scandinavian language
• Experience in writing publications
• Experience in a biosafety level-2 laboratory environment
In the assessment, the emphasis is on the applicant's potential to complete a research education based on the master's thesis or equivalent, and any other scientific work. (The motivation letter will also be considered.) In addition, professional experience and other experience of significance for the completion of the doctoral programme will be taken into consideration.

We will also emphasize motivation and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have good collaboration skills
• Have good communication and interaction with colleagues and students
• Wants to contribute to a good working environment
As many people as possible should have the opportunity to undertake organized research training. If you already hold a PhD or have equivalent competence, we will not appoint you to this position.
Admission to the PhD programme 
For employment in the PhD position, you must be qualified for admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Health Sciences and participate in organized doctoral studies within the employment period.

Admission normally requires:  

• A bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS and a master's degree of 120 ECTS, or an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 30 ECTS for a master's degree of 120 ECTS. 
• A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 20 ECTS for an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
 
 
Applicants must have a grade of C or better on the master's thesis and have a grade point average of C or better for the master's degree. A more detailed description of admission requirements can be found here.

If you are employed in the position, you will be provisionally admitted to the PhD programme. Application for final admission must be submitted no later than two months after taking up the position. 

Applicants with a foreign education will be subjected to an evaluation of whether the educational background is equal to Norwegian higher education, following national guidelines from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills. Depending on which country the education is from, one or two additional years of university education may be required to fulfil admission requirements, e.g. a 4-year bachelor's degree and a 2-year master's degree. UiT normally accepts higher education from countries that are part of the Lisbon Recognition Convention.
Inclusion and diversity
UiT The Arctic University of Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity are a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite at least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.
We offer
• Involvement in an interesting research project 
• Good career opportunities 
• A good academic environment with dedicated colleagues  
• Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
• Pension scheme through the state pension fund 
• PhD Fellows are normally given a salary of 580 000 NOK/year with a 3% yearly increase
Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information about working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility
Application 
Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include: 

• A motivation letter describing how this position aligns with the applicant’s research interests.
• CV, including a list of publications, if applicable. 
• Official diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language 
• Official transcripts of grades/academic record for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language
• Official translation of diplomas and transcripts of records (ToR) to English or a Scandinavian language, if applicable
• Explanation of the grading system for foreign education (Diploma Supplement if available)
• Documentation of English proficiency
• Two references with contact information
Qualification with a master’s degree is required before commencement in the position. If you are near completion of your master’s degree, you may still apply and submit a statement from your supervisor or institution indicating when the degree will be obtained. You must still submit your transcript of grades for the master’s degree with your application.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 
Assessment 
The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. 
General information 
The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants. 

Remuneration for the position of PhD Fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017. A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension: You may be entitled to financial support if you become ill or disabled, your family may be entitled to financial support when you die, you become insured against occupational injury or occupational disease, and you can get good terms on a mortgage. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.
 
A shorter period of appointment may be decided when the PhD Fellow has already completed parts of their research training programme or when the appointment is based on a previous qualifying position PhD Fellow, research assistant, or the like in such a way that the total time used for research training amounts to three years. 

We process personal data given in an application or CV in accordance with the Personal Data Act (Offentleglova). According to the Personal Data Act information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. You will receive advance notification in the event of such publication, if you have requested non-disclosure. 

 

Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is a multi-campus research university and the northernmost university of the world. Our central location in the High North, our broad and diverse research and study portfolio, and our interdisciplinary qualities make us uniquely suited to meet the challenges of the future. At UiT you can explore global issues from a close-up perspective.

Credibility, academic freedom, closeness, creativity and commitment shall be hallmarks of the relationship between our employees, between our employees and our students and between UiT and our partners.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at UiT The Arctic University of Norway represents a newly created entity gathering almost all possible health study programs. This facilitates an unique interdisciplinarity and innovation in health education and research. We work closely with the services in the North to solve tomorrow's challenges.
 
Read more about us at uit.no/helsefak

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellowships in Mathematical Sciences
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,600 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

     
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We have a vacancy for up to two postdoctoral fellowships at the Department of Mathematical Sciences.

The purpose of a postdoctoral position is to build up a researcher profile that qualifies for a position as associate professor. The position may also offer additional skills that are relevant to the postdoctoral fellow's future career.

The Department of Mathematical Sciences wants to support excellent and highly motivated candidates within any of the Department's main research disciplines; please see https://www.ntnu.edu/imf/research/ for an overview.

The positions must start no later than October 1st, 2027.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
Duties of the position
• Carry out high quality research.
• Academic publications.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign academic institutions.
• Teaching and other duties.Required selection criteria
• You must have completed a doctoral degree in one of the research areas of the Department. If you are in the final phase of your doctorate and can document that the thesis has been submitted or that the defense date has been confirmed, your application can be considered even if you have not defended. NOTE: Documentation of the obtained doctorate must be presented before you can take up the position.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in English.
PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”.

If you do not already have educational competence that meets the requirements for a position as associate professor in Norway, NTNU will arrange for you to acquire such competence during the employment period. In such cases, you will also be assigned relevant teaching as part of the career-promoting work.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions and for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Preference will be given to candidates who have a strong potential to strengthen the current research areas, or can provide a bridge between the different research activities in the department.
• Experience with teaching.Personal characteristics
• Motivation for conducting research at an advanced level.
• Ability to work independently and in a team.
• Good communication skills.
• Motivation for teaching.
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer 
• An exciting job with an important social mission.
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment.
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues.
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.
• Free Norwegian language training.
As a Postdoctoral Fellow at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
As a Postdoctoral Fellow (code 1352) you are normally paid from gross NOK 667 000,- per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. From the salary, 2% is deducted as a contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The period of employment is 3 years (including 1 year of career promotion work/ teaching duties).

As an employee at NTNU, it is important to keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and to adapt to them. 

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed
About the application 
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above.

The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. 

The application must include:

• A project plan written together with a permanent scientific employee (who will act as a mentor) at the Department (maximum 800 words/2 pages).
• A brief statement from the potential mentor that they are willing to host the proposed project.
• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's-,Master's- and PhD degrees. If you have not yet completed your PhD, you must provideconfirmation on your estimated date for the doctoral dissertation, or confirmation that your PhD thesis has been submitted.
• Documentation of a completed doctoral degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• CV, including information about teaching experience, if applicable.
• Academic works - published or unpublished (up to 5 items).
• Name and contact information of three referees.
If all or parts of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education. Description of the documentation required can be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.Joint works will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint works, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

If you have had leave or another break in your career, it is important that this is stated in your application so that the selection committee can take this into account and that the amount of your research may be reduced as a result.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal qualities. Motivation, ambitions and potential for research will also be emphasized in the assessment of the candidates.

NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and is committed to follow evaluation criteria for research quality according to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment DORA and the obligations in CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information 
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public list of applicants, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact Marte P. H. Andresen (marte.andresen@ntnu.no).

If you find this position interesting, and in accordance with your qualifications, please submit your application electronically via jobbnorge.no with your CV, diplomas and certificates attached.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Back in 1986, two very passionate skiers, one of them a world-class mogul skier with several World Cup wins, were sitting next to each other in a chairlift heading up a mountain. About to test and write about a new skiwear line, they started to talk about why no one was making skiwear that they wanted to wear. Garments that combined excellent functionality with simple, attractive design. Also, they wondered if there was any way that they could stay longer and more often in the ski resort they both loved - the little mountain village Åre, in northern Sweden.  

It turned out that the answer to both questions was Peak Performance. Initially, their ambitions didn’t extend much beyond making some clothes for themselves and their friends, in sufficient quantities to make a living from it. The business was shaped by what was important to them. Finding the right design and technical solution was paramount.

And the strategy worked. In the late 1980’s, people were tired of extravagance and superficiality. Everybody was looking for the real thing that comes with genuine quality. Ski jackets with leather details and flannel shirts were suddenly the answer, rather than neon and looking like a fully decorated Christmas tree. Orders generated by the first mail order catalog overwhelmed the little post office in town. So much so that they had to take on more staff just to keep up.  

During the early years, most things took longer to do than they should have. After all, Peak Performance was a company founded by skiers – people who more than anything else wanted to ski some winter. Anyone who managed to find our little office in Åre was often confronted with a sign on the front door that read: Gone skiing.

Global Test Engineer / Technician – Production test 

We are looking for a technically skilled and independent colleague to support our production sites around the world in testing, test processes, training, and follow-up activities. 

The position involves extensive travel and extended stays at our production sites. The core responsibility is to train and guide local personnel, ensure that testing is carried out in accordance with our procedures, and contribute to consistent, high-quality standards across all locations. 

You will work hands-on with test stations and equipment, provide technical support when issues arise, and ensure that local teams understand both how tests are performed and how the equipment is operated and maintained. 

Key Responsibilities 

• Travel to production sites worldwide and support local teams in performing tests and following established test processes. 
• Train and guide operators and technical personnel in test methodologies, operation of test stations, equipment, and software. 
• Ensure that testing is performed in accordance with established procedures, specifications, and quality requirements. 
• Support the installation, commissioning, and implementation of test equipment and test processes at new and existing production sites. 
• Troubleshoot, install, verify, and maintain test stations and associated equipment. 
• Document faults, deviations, and solutions, and follow up on corrective actions. 
• Collaborate with central engineering teams and technical specialists when issues require specialized expertise. 
• Prepare and configure PCs, standardized system images, and test software, and assist with basic network troubleshooting. 
• Develop and improve test instructions, user manuals, and training materials. 
• Share experiences and lessons learned from production sites with central testing, development, and engineering teams, contributing to more robust and standardized test setups. 
Qualifications and Requirements  

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent technical education in electrical engineering, automation, electronics, mechatronics, control systems, IT, or a related field. Relevant qualification combined with extensive practical experience in production, testing, technical service, or industrial environments may be considered equivalent to higher education. 
• Good technical understanding of test equipment and production processes, with a systematic approach to troubleshooting. 
• Familiarity with PCs, software installation, and standardized system configurations, as well as a basic understanding of networking. 
• Interest in IT/OT systems and how production IT supports testing and manufacturing operations. 
• Ability to follow technical procedures and quality requirements. 
• Good written and verbal communication skills in both Norwegian and English. English is the primary working language in our global projects. 
• To be considered for the position, you must be eligible to obtain a security clearance in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act.
Experience in a production environment, technical testing, or working with test equipment is an advantage, as is previous experience in technical training or travel-based technical support roles. 

You do not need to be an IT/OT or networking specialist. What matters most is that you are comfortable with hands-on troubleshooting and enjoy learning new systems and technologies. 

Personal Qualities 

You have strong communication and training skills, enjoy sharing knowledge, and are able to explain technical processes clearly and effectively. You work independently, take initiative, and approach challenges in a calm, solution-oriented, and methodical way, even when working on your own in the field. With a hands-on and practical approach, you enjoy working directly with technical equipment and solving practical technical challenges. You are structured and organized, follow established procedures, and ensure accurate documentation of your work. You are also adaptable and culturally aware, with the ability to build strong working relationships across different cultures, teams, and locations. As the role involves frequent international travel and extended stays at production sites abroad, you must be comfortable with both. 
Location: Kongsberg. The role involves a significant amount of travel.
What We Offer 

This is a varied and hands-on technical role with extensive international exposure, offering the opportunity to work with test equipment, production processes, and technical solutions across multiple countries. You will play a key role in training colleagues and ensuring consistent testing quality across our global production sites, while working closely with production, testing, IT, and engineering teams. The role also offers excellent opportunities for professional development, as well as the chance to influence and improve testing processes and working methods. 

 

About Us 

Division Missiles & Aerostructures is part of Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace. We develop, assemble, test, and deliver advanced missile systems for naval vessels, coastal defense systems, helicopters, and fighter aircraft. 

Increasing activity and international demand are driving significant growth across our missile business and production organization. Expanding production capacity across locations requires us to develop and transfer critical manufacturing expertise effectively and consistently. 

 

Important Information 

Candidates applying for this position will undergo a background check as part of the recruitment process. The outcome will be considered as part of the overall assessment. 

To be considered for the position, you must be eligible to obtain a security clearance in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act. 

Please note that the recruitment process will continue in January.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship within Predictive Runtime Verification of AI-enabled Robotic Autonomous Systems
jobs.employer_name: NORGES MILJØ- OG BIOVITENSKAPELIGE UNIVERSITET (NMBU) CAMPUS ÅS
jobs.description:
About the position
A PhD position is available in the Robotics Group at the Faculty of Science and Technology.

The PhD position is for a period of 3 years, with a desired start date of 1st of January 2026.

Recent advances in AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) bring major challenges regarding safety, uncertainty management, accountability, and runtime assurance in autonomous robotic systems. Operating in safety-critical, highly complex, dynamic, and hostile environments require systems to maintain formal safety guarantees while optimizing operational efficiency.

As a selected candidate for the announced PhD position, you will research and develop novel, context-aware, AI-enabled Predictive Runtime Verification (PRV) frameworks and adaptive monitors. By anticipating anomalies or failures before they occur, your research will enable proactive corrective actions and real-time replanning in robotic autonomous systems.

The PhD position is part of the research project PREVAIL - Predictive Runtime Verification of AI-enabled Systems, funded by the Research Council of Norway (RCN). The project builds upon scientific foundations established in the RoboFarmer project and is conducted in close strategic partnership with the Norwegian Defence University College (FHS) who will also serve as co-supervisor for the candidate and provide opportunity for research stay at FHS.
 
In addition, the PhD work will provide ample opportunity to conduct research in collaboration with international academic partners, most notably at Académie Militaire de Saint-Cyr Coëtquidan, France, University of York, UK and Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) in Stockholm, Sweden. The PREVAIL project will encourage the selected PhD candidate and provide opportunities to benefit intellectually from interaction and extended visits with internationally recognized researchers and institutes.

This PhD position is funded through the Research Council of Norway's call Supplementary Funding for Ongoing Projects to Enhance Knowledge and Results Transfer from ICT Research to the Defence Sector. The funding scheme requires candidates to be eligible for security clearance at a minimum level of "Secret". As the project is expected to involve research subject to Norwegian export control regulations, appointment is contingent upon the successful candidate obtaining the required security clearance and any necessary export control licences or approvals.
Main tasks
• Survey state-of-the-art AI-enabled Predictive Runtime Verification (PRV) methodologies and analyze their suitability for defence-oriented, safety-critical, autonomous robotic applications. 
• Formulate and develop novel algorithms, formal methodologies, and tools for context-aware PRV and AI-enhanced monitor synthesis.
• Conduct a research stay at the Norwegian Defence University College (FHS) to align research with the domain-specific requirements and preferences.
• Integrate PRV frameworks with adaptive risk-mitigation, failure avoidance, and real-time replanning mechanisms.
• Perform early-phase prototyping, software implementation (e.g., ROS 2), and testing on robotic platforms in defence-relevant environments and scenarios.
• Author scientific papers for presentation at international high-impact conferences and peer-reviewed journals.
• Complete mandatory PhD coursework and seminars in accordance with NMBU doctoral regulations.Competence
Required qualifications

• A Master's degree or equivalent in Robotics, Computer Science, Cybernetics, Formal Methods, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. Foreign degrees must correspond with the admission criteria for the PhD program. Candidates submitting M.Sc. thesis within the application deadline may be considered.
• In the Master’s degree, both the average grade point and the Master’s thesis, must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system. Applicants who have recently graduated with excellent results may be given preference.
• Proficiency in both written and oral English in correspondence with the admission criteria for the PhD program.
• Solid knowledge and background in at least two of the following fields: Formal Methods / Runtime Verification, AI / Machine Learning, Autonomous Systems / Control, or Software Development for Robotics (e.g., ROS/ROS 2). 
• Strong programming skills (Python, C++, etc.) 
• The successful candidate must be eligible for security clearance at a minimum level of "Secret" and any licences or approvals required under Norwegian export control legislation
• Personal suitability and motivation for the position.
Qualifications considered an advantage

• Experience with formal verification, model-checking, runtime monitoring, and/or temporal logic synthesis. 
• Experience with AI models, Large Language Models (LLMs), or reinforcement learning integrated into robotic control loops.
• Experience with safety assurance, risk analysis, adaptive systems, or research involving real-world autonomous applications.
• Practical experience working with physical mobile robotic hardware, sensors, and simulation environments.
• Previous research and peer-reviewed publications within these domains.
Personal qualities

• Be curios, result-oriented and highly motivated
• Possess strong communication and cooperation skills
• Have a solid interest in robotics
• Good collaboration skills and an ability to join interdisciplinary academic/industrial communitiesRemuneration and further information
Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017, 550 800 NOK. For exceptionally well qualified candidates a higher salary may be considered. 

By applying, the candidate confirms that information and documentation submitted via the job application may also be used by NMBU in a possible admission process to the PhD program. Admission to a PhD program is a prerequisite for appointment to the PhD position.

For professional and social interactions, the candidate is expected to be physically present at NMBU on a daily basis.

jobs.description:
Do you want to build and lead the team that will develop and transfer missile production expertise across KONGSBERG's global manufacturing network? 

We are looking for an experienced and ambitious Team Manager to establish and lead our new Global Missile Production Training department within Strategic Production, Division Missiles & Aerostructures (DMA). 

As our global production footprint expands, developing people and transferring critical production expertise across sites will be essential to our continued growth. 

You will build the team and establish a scalable approach to production training for Naval Strike Missile (NSM) and Joint Strike Missile (JSM) in Norway and internationally. You will lead a multidisciplinary team with expertise in missile assembly, painting, inspection, testing, and technical support. 

Your Mission 

Your primary mission is to establish Global Missile Production Training as a high-performing team and a trusted partner to our production organization. You will lead by example, creating an environment where people take ownership, share expertise, collaborate effectively, and continuously improve. 

You will: 

• Build, lead, and develop a multidisciplinary production training team. 
• Recruit and develop skilled employees and create a strong culture of trust, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
• Plan and coordinate training activities in Norway and across international production sites. 
• Translate production needs and growth ambitions into competence requirements, training priorities, and resource plans. 
• Work closely with production management and subject-matter experts to develop and continuously improve training programs, materials, methods, and processes. 
• Drive standardization and effective knowledge transfer across locations while maintaining production and quality requirements. 
• Manage staffing, capacity, competence, and resources. 
• Build strong relationships with production leaders and stakeholders across disciplines and international sites. 
• Monitor progress, risks, and capability gaps and communicate priorities and challenges to management. 
• Ensure compliance with relevant requirements and regulations, in Norway and internationally. 
International travel will be an important part of the role. During periods of lower training demand, the team will support missile production in Norway, maintaining a strong connection between training expertise and hands-on production experience. 

Who We Are Looking For 

We are looking for a leader who combines strong people leadership, operational understanding, and the ambition to build something new. 

You understand that competence is a critical production capability and that successful industrial growth depends on our ability to develop people and transfer knowledge effectively across teams, cultures, and locations. You are comfortable setting direction and leading through others while staying close enough to operations to understand what makes production succeed. 

We believe you bring: 

• Solid experience in people leadership and team development. 
• Experience from production, manufacturing, or another complex operational environment. 
• The ability to translate strategic and operational needs into clear priorities and executable plans. 
• A strong understanding of the relationship between competence, training, quality, and production performance. 
• Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills across disciplines, locations, and cultures. 
• A structured and proactive leadership style, combined with sound judgement and a strong drive for results. 
• Strong communication skills in both Norwegian and English, written and spoken. 
• Good digital skills and confidence using relevant IT tools. 
Experience from KONGSBERG production environments is an advantage. 

Why Join Us? 

This is more than an opportunity to lead an established operation. You will have the opportunity to build a new capability that will contribute directly to the future growth of our missile production organization. 

You will help shape how production expertise is developed and shared, how new personnel build the competence required to produce NSM and JSM, and how we scale production internationally while maintaining high standards of quality and performance. 

You will join a high-tech, international organization experiencing significant growth, with excellent opportunities to develop your leadership capabilities, professional expertise, and international network. 

We offer competitive salary and benefits, including pension and insurance schemes, employee share programs, and bonus arrangements. 

Employees also have access to training facilities and an innovation center featuring drones, laser cutters, 3D printers, and VR technology, as well as cabin rentals and other employee welfare benefits. 

About Us 

Division Missiles & Aerostructures is part of Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace. We develop, assemble, test, and deliver advanced missile systems for naval vessels, coastal defense systems, helicopters, and fighter aircraft. 

Increasing activity and international demand are driving significant growth across our missile business and production organization. Expanding production capacity across locations requires us to develop and transfer critical manufacturing expertise effectively and consistently. 

Important Information 

Candidates applying for this position will undergo a background check as part of the recruitment process. The outcome will be considered as part of the overall assessment. 

To be considered for the position, you must be eligible to obtain a security clearance in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act. 

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. 

Please note that the recruitment process will continue in January.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Materials Physics
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Studies of the microstructural origin of ductility in recycled aluminium alloys 

The position is a 3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in the autumn of 2027. The PhD candidate will be a part of the TEM Gemini Centre,  and the characterization activities in SFI FAST, working in close collaboration with project partners from NTNU and SINTEF, and with leading Norwegian and international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain.

The PhD candidate will investigate how microstructural constituents influence plastic deformation, strain localisation and ductile fracture in recycled aluminium alloys. The project aims to establish a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms governing ductility in alloys produced with increasing amounts of post-consumer scrap, where complex microstructures arise from variations in alloy chemistry, thermomechanical processing and impurity content.

The research will combine advanced electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and mechanical testing to characterise microstructural features across multiple length scales, including precipitates, precipitate-free zones, grain boundaries, constituent particles and deformation-induced defect structures. Particular emphasis will be placed on understanding how these microstructural constituents interact during deformation and how they affect strain localisation, damage evolution and fracture.

The project builds on previous work performed within the TEM Gemini Centre and SFI FAST and will be carried out in close collaboration with researchers in materials physics and solid mechanics at NTNU and SINTEF. The PhD candidate will work closely with experts in advanced microscopy, deformation experiments and microstructure-based modelling, contributing to the development of future recycled aluminium alloys with improved mechanical performance.

The starting date is August or September 2027. Requests for an earlier or later starting date may be considered and must be stated in the application.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures 
SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminium industry. The centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 15 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. SFI FAST runs from 2026 to 2033 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy. 

The primary objective of SFI FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance. 

A key outcome of SFI FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains. 

Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. 5 PhD students started in 2026.

Please see the centre’s website: Future Aluminium Structures (FAST) - NTNU
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate degree
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Conduct and publish high-level research in peer-reviewed journals
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Contribute to popular science dissemination
• Participate in the TEM Gemini Centre and SFI FAST research groups 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Investigate how microstructural constituents such as precipitates, precipitate-free zones, grain boundaries and constituent particles influence deformation, strain localisation and ductility in recycled aluminium alloys.
• Plan and perform advanced microstructural characterisation using state-of-the-art electron microscopy and related techniques, including TEM, STEM, SEM, EBSD and diffraction-based methods.
• Correlate microstructure with mechanical behaviour through quantitative analysis and close interaction with modelling activities in collaboration with researchers in solid mechanics and fracture modelling.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Physics, Nanotechnology, Materials Science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than September 2027. 
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in English
• Experience with experimental work within physics, nanotechnology or material science.
• Basic programming skills.
• The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.Preferred selection criteria
• Hands-on experience with materials characterisation using electron microscopy techniques, preferably (S)TEM and/or SEM/EBSD.
• Interest in microstructure-property relationships, deformation mechanisms and mechanical behaviour of metallic materials.
• Interest and experience in working with industrial problems.
• Experience with image analysis, programming or quantitative data processing (in Python) is an advantage.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• Participation in a new innovative research centre, in an international work environment involving SINTEF and key industrial European partners in the aluminium value chain.
• Collaboration with leading experts in advanced material science, addressing highly relevant industrial and societal challenges for European industries.
• Training and access to state-of-the-art instruments at the TEM Gemini Centre /NORTEM Trondheim node.
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)  
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Physics within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• CV
• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• If you have finished your master’s degree, include a copy of the master's thesis. 
• If you have recently submitted, or not yet submitted, your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of two relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement fromNorwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. 

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Randi Holmestad, email randi.holmestad@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Consultant Anja Isaksen, e-mail: anja.t.isaksen@ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 01.12.2026

jobs.occupation: Researcher in Pore Scale Reservoir Engineering - IV-82/26
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the Job
We have a vacancy for research position of 12 months at the Department of Geosciences (IGV) at NTNU within the group Well and Reservoir (former Reservoir Engineering and Petrophysics). The position is funded by PoreLab and organized under the Department of Geosciences. The position will be situated within the Center of Excellence PoreLab, which will give excellent opportunities for collaboration and development on a personal and scientific level. For the position as a researcher, the goal is to develop experimental proof to validate theoretical predictions for multiphase fluid flow characterization at the Darcy scale.

The researcher will work in close collaboration with associate professor Antje van der Net and professors Alex Hansen and Carl Fredrik Berg. 

Your immediate leader is the head of the department in IGV. 
Duties of the position
• The area of interest is multiphase fluid flow description at pore level using pore scale imaging. 
• The objective of the research work is to verify the newly developed theory for multiphase flow in porous media based on equilibrium thermodynamics using entropy as flow descriptor. This requires imaging of spatial fluid distribution under different flow conditions and porous media characteristics.
• The validation shall be done using experimental methods supported by numerical modelling tools. The work might require development of new experimental methodsRequired selection criteria
• Minimum a PhD in a relevant subject area STEM, preferably related to fluid mechanics and transport in porous media. 
• A strong background in thermodynamics is preferred as well as experimental experience in a fluid mechanics laboratory and imaging techniques
• Good written and oral English. Preferred selection criteria
• Strong analytical thinking
• Good communication and presentation skills
• Norwegian language skills are advantageousPersonal characteristics
• The position requires a high level of self-responsibility including own initiative and critical thinking.
• The candidate shall have the ability to work independently where self motivation and ambition are crucial 
• The candidate shall be flexible, creative and open for new ideas, and have an ability for self-reflection and should enjoy interdisciplinary research in an intercultural team.
• Being disciplined and well organized are preferred.
Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities.
We offer
• exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
• an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
• favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• employee benefitsSalary and conditions
As a researcher (code 1109) you are paid depending on qualifications and senority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU.   

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work. 

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. 
About the application
Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. 

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your application must include:

• CV, diplomas, and certificates
• Academic works – published or unpublished – that you wish to be considered during assessment of your application (up to 10 items)
• A description of the scientific/artistic works you consider most relevant, which you particularly wish to be factored into the assessment
• A complete publication list
• Details of projects for which you have served as project manager, including information on financing, duration, and scope
• Names and contact information for three relevant referees
It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for  documentation of your competence.

Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions. 

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and The obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.
General information
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.   

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.  

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. 

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. 

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Associate Professor Antje van der Net, e-mail: antje.van.der.net@ntnu.no. 

If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact Senior Adviser HR, e-mail: eli.meistad@ntnu.no
