jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Multi-Robot Informative Planning for Coastal Monitoring
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of ICT and Natural Sciences (IIR) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) in Ålesund is opening a PhD position in distributed informative planning for teams of autonomous and remotely operated marine vehicles, with applications in coastal environmental monitoring.

Coastal waters and fjords change continuously. Pollutants spread, floating litter drifts with wind and currents, and water quality and biological activity vary across both space and time. A single vehicle can only observe a small part of such an environment at once. Teams of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), supported by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), can cover larger areas, observe processes from several viewpoints at the same time, and respond to what they detect.

To use such teams effectively, the vehicles must build a shared and predictive picture of the environment and decide together where each of them should go next. They must do this under the real constraints of the marine environment, including limited communication, changing weather and heterogeneous vehicles.

The position is part of NTNU Ålesund’s work on ocean intelligence: collecting data about the ocean to support use cases such as monitoring of fish spawning grounds, mapping of microplastics and suspended contamination and water quality monitoring. 

The position builds on ongoing research at the department on autonomous surface vehicles, informative path planning, online mapping of spatial fields and tracking of drifting targets, which has been validated in field trials. The PhD project will extend these methods from single vehicles to cooperating teams of heterogeneous vehicles.

The research will combine theory, simulation and field experiments. Field work will be carried out in coastal waters near Ålesund with the department's fleet of USVs and UAVs.

The successful candidate will contribute to one or more of the following areas:

• Multi-robot coordination for monitoring spatially and temporally varying phenomena, such as drifting objects, pollutant plumes and evolving environmental fields, including distributed informative path and trajectory planning.
• Mobile robot sensing, mapping and active decision making for heterogeneous teams of USVs and UAVs, using methods such as model predictive control, sampling-based planning, probabilistic mapping and machine learning, under limited and intermittent communication.
• Implementation on real vehicles and validation in field experiments, including remote operation and supervision of the team
Within the scope of the project, the PhD research can be adapted to the candidate's interests and background, with emphasis on planning and control, estimation and mapping, or learning-based methods.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral training programme and successfully obtain a PhD degree.
• Conduct high-quality research within the framework described above.
• Develop, implement and test algorithms in simulation and on real vehicles.
• Plan and take part in field experiments with teams of USVs and UAVs.
• Contribute to academic publications and engage in popular science dissemination.
• Actively participate in the research group Cyber-Physical Systems Laboratory (CPS Lab).
• Engage in international academic activities, including conferences and/or research stays at partner institutions abroad.
• Take courses in relevant technical topics, comprising a minimum of 30 ECTS.Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in engineering cybernetics, robotics, control engineering, marine technology, mechatronics or a closely related field. Candidates with strong backgrounds in computer science, applied mathematics or data science combined with relevant experience in robotics, optimization or machine learning will also be considered. 
• Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education.
• You must have good programming skills, for example in Python or C++.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's doctoral programme in Engineering Cybernetics.
• Applicants from non-English speaking countries outside Europe must present an official language test report. The acceptable tests are TOEFL, IELTS, and Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) or Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE).
• Minimum scores are:
• TOEFL: 600 / writing 4.5 (paper-based) or 92 / writing 22 (internet-based)
• IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted)
• CAE/CPE: grade B or A. 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Experience with multi-agent or multi-robot systems, distributed optimization or distributed estimation
• Experience with informative path planning, model predictive control or sampling-based planning
• Experience with Gaussian processes or other probabilistic mapping methods
• Experience with ROS/ROS2, robotics simulators such as Gazebo, or GPU-accelerated computing
• Experience with field work, marine vehicles or drones
• Drone pilot certificate (EU A1/A3 or A2) and/or boat driving license for Norway
• Demonstrated research ability, e.g. through publications, thesis work, technical reports or open-source contributions.
• Relevant industry or applied research experience.
The research activity may lead to using sensitive information or insights into critical infrastructure that is subject to specific security restrictions. Restrictions could also include obtaining a formal security clearance according to the Norwegian Security Act. Non-Norwegian citizens can be granted clearance. However, candidates from non-EEA or non-NATO countries can not expect to obtain a security clearance.
Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to:

• Work independently and in a structured way, as well as collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team
• Communicate effectively and present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed 
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
 

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years, with the possibility of up to 12 months additional employment related to career-enhancing activities.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering Cybernetics within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• CV and certificates.
• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees.
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page).
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages).
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work.
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees. 
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Erlend Magnus Lervik Coates (erlend.coates@ntnu.no). 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact Silje Storbråten Kjersem (silje.s.kjersem@ntnu.no).

jobs.occupation: Want to take ownership of the technology behind smarter business spending?
jobs.description:
At Done Spend, you’ll build the features and integrations that help businesses manage corporate cards, capture expenses and control spending in real time.

As our Full Stack Engineer, you’ll take ownership of core platform components, contribute to architectural decisions and follow your work from initial idea through to deployment. Working closely with our Technical Lead and Product team, you’ll help shape how features are built and how the platform develops.

For this role, we welcome candidates who would like to work from either our Oslo, Stockholm or Skövde office.

What you’ll work on

Your work will span frontend development, backend services and integrations. Alongside building new features, you’ll improve the reliability, security and performance of the platform businesses use to manage their spending.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Building and maintaining secure, scalable frontend and backend components.
• Developing API integrations, authentication flows, webhooks and data synchronisation processes.
• Contributing to technical design and assessing the feasibility of new features with Product.
• Writing unit and integration tests, investigating bugs and improving performance and monitoring.
• Maintaining clear technical documentation and identifying opportunities to improve automation and reliability.
You’ll also contribute to sprint planning and retrospectives, helping the team improve how it delivers software.
What you’ll bring
You have 2 to 4 years of experience building production applications and can work across both frontend and backend development.

We’re looking for:

• Strong JavaScript and TypeScript skills, with experience writing production code across the stack.
• Experience in fintech, particularly payments or spend management, is a strong advantage. 
• Experience with React and modern single-page application frameworks.
• Experience with NestJS or a comparable structured backend framework, such as .NET.
• Experience building and consuming RESTful APIs and/or working with event-driven systems.
• Experience with PostgreSQL, solid SQL fundamentals and confidence working with raw SQL, query builders and ORMs.
• An understanding of maintainable code, separation of concerns and scalable system design.
• Strong spoken English skills are required
You’re comfortable working in an Agile team and discussing technical decisions with colleagues across engineering and product . You consider how your code will be tested, maintained and operated after deployment, and take responsibility for resolving issues.

React Native experience is required.
Why join Done Spend?
• Own meaningful parts of the platform. Take responsibility for core components, from feature development to architectural decisions.
• Influence technical direction. Work closely with the Technical Lead, Product team and leadership as the platform grows.
• Build across the stack. Work on user-facing features, backend services and the integrations that connect them.
• See your work in use. Build and improve systems that support real business spending and transactions.
• Choose between Oslo, Stockholm or Skövde. We welcome candidates who would like to work from either office.About Done Spend
Done Spend is part of the Done.ai group and is building an expense management platform for growing companies. By combining smart corporate cards, automated expense capture and real-time financial controls, we help businesses manage how they spend, track and control their money.

As the platform grows, reliable systems and thoughtful engineering are central to the experience we deliver.

Interested in helping shape the next phase of Done Spend? We’d like to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: PhD candidate in Artistic Research – Digital Environments
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Trondheim Academy of Fine Art (KIT), Faculty of Architecture and Design, invites applications for a fixed-term, three-year PhD position in Artistic Research. The PhD will be part of the focus area Digital Environments within Artistic Research.

This PhD position explores, through artistic and practice-based research, the role and societal impact of AI and other emerging technologies, including how digital technologies reshape the relationships between knowledge production, creative practice, accountability, and social and ecological transformation.

The position contributes to artistic research, critical inquiry, and experimentation across AI, sensing, data analysis and visualisation, and investigative practices, addressing key societal challenges at the intersection of art, architecture, design, media, and technology. Embedded in KIT’s strategic focus on the role of art in addressing societal change, the position is connected to ongoing research initiatives, digital infrastructure, and externally funded projects. It will strengthen KIT’s research profile in digitalisation and societal transformation while supporting future national and international research collaborations and funding opportunities. 

As a PhD Candidate, you will work towards a doctorate while gaining valuable research experience and qualifications for a career in higher education, research, and related sectors.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
Duties of the position
You will develop an independent artistic and practice-based research project within the overall scope of the position. The project should engage with at least one of the first two areas below and at least one of the last two, without being limited to them:

1. Investigative practices, including open-source, scientific, data-driven and participatory approaches.2. Sensing, analysis, modelling, visualisation and communication of disparate data and digital environments, through approaches including critical spatial practice and data science.3. Technology in the public interest, including accountability and community-centred approaches to emerging technologies.4. The role of artistic research in the development and application of emerging technologies, including new forms of knowledge production and collaboration between artistic, scientific and technological research. 

The successful candidate will contribute to and make use of the research infrastructure of the Artistic Research Sensing and Visualisation Lab (ARSV-Lab), which develops technological resources and knowledge in multi-perspective sensing and data visualisation.You will have opportunities to participate in relevant existing externally funded research projects and networks, including the ERC project Sensing Ecocide and the COST Action Artistic Intelligence, and to contribute to the wider research environment and research culture of the department.You will participate in the Norwegian Artistic Research School (NARS) as part of their obligatory training component, alongside other candidates in Norwegian PhD programmes in Artistic Research.- Complete doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate- Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above- Academic publications and popular science dissemination- Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions- Other career-promoting work

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Doctoral Programme for Artistic Research PHKUNST, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. 
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in art, architecture, design or a closely related field, or equivalent qualifications. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Demonstrated experience or interest in artistic, practice-based or interdisciplinary approaches to digital technologies, and digital environments.
• Demonstrated ability to pursue independent, mentored research and work collaboratively with interdisciplinary research team.
• Track record in artistic research and/or relevant professional practice at an international level.
• Strong command of both written and spoken English is a prerequisite. 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Personal characteristics
• Excellent communications and teamwork skills 
• Work independently 
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them 
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals 
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback 
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Artistic research within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• A cover letter 
• A preliminary PhD project proposal (3 – 5 pages) 
• CV, certificates and diplomas 
• A portfolio or other relevant documentation 
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
Please do not include full publications or other scientific/artistic works as separate attachments.

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Nabil Ahmed, telephone: +47 403 14 215, email nabil.ahmed@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR advisor Natalia Swahn, e-mail: Natalia.swahn@ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 31.12.2026

Trondheim is the tech capital of Norway with a population of 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens and overall equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized day-care for children is easily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers great opportunities for education (including international schools) and possibilities to enjoy nature, culture and family life and has low crime rates and clean air quality.

jobs.occupation: PhD within Power System & regional PV modelling
jobs.description:
The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) have a vacant PhD research fellowship focused on modelling how increasing photovoltaic (PV) generation affects Norwegian power grids. The position is part of the KSP project Solvar and the Norwegian PV Research Centre (FME SOLAR) and combines regional PV production modelling with power system analysis to support safe and cost-effective integration of solar power. 

The Departments of Solar Power Systems and Energy System Analysis at IFE conduct research on PV systems analysis (including performance and forecasting of PV plants), and energy system modelling (including techno-economic modelling and power flow analysis). The candidate will be supervised by a team of researchers from IFE and the University of Oslo with strong competence in the generation and distribution of electricity. The PhD will be affiliated with the Department of Technology Systems at the University of Oslo.

The PhD candidate will work on robust power grids and regional PV production profiles. The research will develop realistic regional PV models adapted to Norwegian conditions and integrate them into power system models of selected real use cases in the distribution grid. Particular attention will be given to spatial smoothing, simultaneity and ramping of distributed PV, reliable grid integration of PV, as well as the interaction between PV, wind power and run-of-river hydropower. The results will help grid operators assess hosting capacity, operational risks and suitable measures for integrating more PV. The work will combine physical grid and PV modelling, data analysis and selected data-driven methods. Regional PV profiles may be investigated for spatial scales ranging from individual transformers and feeders to larger regions. Validation will use measured and historical PV data, irradiance data, building information and grid data made available through the project and open data sources.   In addition to being integrated into internationally leading research groups at IFE, the candidate will have the opportunity to collaborate with other world-class research communities, e.g., through the International Energy Agency’s Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme Task 16 & 19, and through contributions to the Pan-European Climate Database.  We are looking for a candidate with an education in electrical engineering, physics, energy technology or similar. The candidate should have strong competence in energy systems, have experience with PV or power systems modelling from before and be highly proficient in spoken and written English. It is also an advantage if the candidate has experience of working with Norwegian PV or grids and is proficient in a Scandinavian language.  We seek a candidate with a positive attitude and good communication skills, who can work independently, but also participate actively in the research group. The position will be in a expanding research field with many actors, requiring an ambitious candidate with strong collaborative qualities. The candidate will work in an active and growing research field at IFE, in a young and social work environment. The start date is flexible and can be agreed upon with the successful candidate, with the possibility of starting as late as August 2027.
    
Job description
• 3 years PhD research fellowship within power system and regional PV modelling
• Develop regional PV production models adapted to Norwegian weather, terrain, building stock and PV-system characteristics
• Validate models using measured PV, irradiance and grid data from Solvar datasets
• Integrate regional PV profiles into power system models of Norwegian grids
• Analyse the interaction between PV and other variable renewable energy sources, including wind power and run-of-river hydropower
• Responsible for establishing and maintaining research infrastructure relevant for the PhD work
• Publish research results in peer-reviewed scientific journals and complete a doctoral thesis
• Communicate and present research results in various fora nationally and internationallyQualification requirements
• MSc in electrical engineering, energy systems, physics, applied mathematics, renewable energy, computer science or a closely related field
• Strong programming skills, preferably in python, Julia or similar programming languages.
• Experience with time-series analysis, numerical modelling, optimisation, statistics or machine learning
• Solid understanding of power systems, energy-system modelling or PV system modelling
• Experience with Norwegian power systems, PV performance in Nordic conditions, snow modelling, or geographical data is a benefit
• Excellent oral and written English
• Understanding of Norwegian is preferablePersonal qualities
• Ability to take initiatives and come up with new ideas
• Analytical, systematic, and thorough
• Excellent collaborative and communicative skills
• Comfortable working across disciplines and with both research and industry partners      We offer
• Work in an industrially relevant and internationally leading research environment
• An informal, positive working environment with friendly and knowledgeable colleagues
• Participation in Ung i IFE, a fun and social network for young employees offering after-work events, weekend trips and scientific seminars
• Close collaboration with the University of Oslo, Norwegian grid operators, the solar industry and international research communities
• Access to unique datasets and use cases from Norwegian distribution grids and PV installations
• Salary according to agreement
• Social benefits including pension, life insurance and accident insurance

This includes questions about any ties to countries that the PST has classified as a ‘high-risk country’ in its open threat assessment. jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate - Hydrogen and Industrial Decarbonization Pathways
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We invite applications for a 3-year PhD Candidate position on the future role of hydrogen and hydrogen products in industrial decarbonization. The position is based at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management, located at NTNU’s campus in Trondheim.

The mission of Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management (IØT) is to carry out education, research, and innovation activities at an international level at the intersection between technology/natural sciences and business economics, management, and HSE. The department’s activities aim to contribute to sustainable value creation within technology-based areas in industry, business, and the public sector in Norway

 

About the position

Electrification is widely promoted as a key pathway to industrial decarbonization. At the same time, hydrogen and carbon capture and storage (CCS) are increasingly recognized as important solutions for sectors where direct electrification may be difficult or uneconomic. This has led to a growing debate about the future role of "electrons versus molecules" in a net-zero economy.

Most existing studies assume that today's industrial structure remains largely unchanged and focus on how current industries can reduce emissions. However, deep decarbonization may fundamentally reshape industrial production, value chains, competitiveness, and the location of energy-intensive activities. As a result, future hydrogen demand may depend as much on industrial transformation as on technological choices.

This PhD project will investigate how alternative pathways toward a zero-emission industrial sector affect the future demand for hydrogen and the development of hydrogen value chains. The research will analyze the interplay between electrification, hydrogen, and CCS, while explicitly accounting for potential changes in industrial structures and production systems.

 

The project addresses research questions like:

• How will future hydrogen demand vary across alternative industrial decarbonization pathways?
• Which industrial sectors are likely to rely on electrification, hydrogen, or CCS to achieve net-zero emissions?
• How might industrial transformation affect hydrogen production, transport, storage, and trade?
• What level of hydrogen deployment is required to justify dedicated hydrogen infrastructure and markets?
• How can Europe and Norway prepare for different industrial and energy-system transition pathways?
 

The successful candidate will develop and analyze future scenarios for industrial transformation, hydrogen demand, and infrastructure development. The project will contribute to the scientific and policy debate on how competitive zero-emission industries can emerge under different transition strategies.
Research environment
The PhD candidate will join a multidisciplinary research environment at the intersection of energy economics, industrial economics, operations research, and energy systems analysis.

The position is affiliated with FME HYDROGENi, the Norwegian Research and Innovation Centre for Hydrogen and Ammonia. The centre brings together 46 research and industry partners to develop the knowledge, technologies, and solutions needed to support a sustainable hydrogen economy and contribute to Norway's ambitions for climate neutrality and industrial transformation. FME HYDROGENi conducts research across the hydrogen value chain, including hydrogen production, transport and storage, industrial and maritime applications, safety, and the broader role of hydrogen in future energy systems. The centre is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research (FME) programme and operates during the period 2022-2030

The PhD candidate will be hosted at the Managerial Economics, Finance and Operations Research (BEDØK) group at the Department of Industrial Economics and Technology Management. The group is one of Norway’s leading academic environments in operations research, logistics, optimization, and quantitative decision support. The candidate will work in close collaboration with researchers from NTNU’s Department of Computer Science and Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Your role in the project
The PhD candidate will:

• Conduct original scientific research on hydrogen and industrial decarbonization pathways.
• Develop and analyze scenarios for industrial transformation and climate neutrality.
• Assess the future role of electrification, hydrogen, and CCS across industrial sectors.
• Quantify hydrogen demand and infrastructure requirements under alternative transition pathways.
• Publish research results in leading international journals and conferences.
• Collaborate with academic, industry, and public-sector partners.
• Complete the required coursework as part of the PhD programme.
• Contribute to dissemination and communication of research findings.
 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Qualification requirements
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant field with strong academic results (B or better according to NTNU’s grading scale). Relevant academic backgrounds include:

• Operations research or optimization
• Energy systems
• Energy Economics
• Engineering disciplines with strong quantitative and analytical content
• Or other closely related disciplines.
Applicants must demonstrate strong analytical and quantitative skills.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Desired qualifications
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:

• Experience with energy system modelling, scenario analysis, or techno-economic analysis.
• Knowledge of hydrogen technologies, industrial decarbonization, or climate policy.
• Experience with quantitative modelling and data analysis.
• Programming skills in Python, Julia, R, GAMS, or similar tools.
• Interest in interdisciplinary research at the interface of technology, economics, and policy.
Applicants in the final phase of their master’s studies are encouraged to apply.
Personal characteristics
We are looking for a candidate who:

• Is intellectually curious and motivated to conduct high-quality research
• Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Works independently and in a structured manner
• Has excellent communication and collaboration skills
• Thrives in an interdisciplinary research environment. 
• Is interested in research with relevance for industry, policy, and society.
Emphasis will be placed on scientific quality, research potential, and personal suitability.
We offer
• An exciting and international academic environment with opportunities for competence development 
• Close collaboration with leading researchers in energy systems modelling, optimization, and something else 
• Opportunities to engage with industry partners and public sector stakeholders
• Participation in research addressing key challenges of the green transition.
• Opportunities for international research stays and conference participation.
• An open and inclusive workplace  with engaged colleagues 
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Employee benefits
• Good loan, insurance, and pension schemes in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund 
• Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
• Working at NTNU 
Information about working and living in Norway can be found at the following link: https://www.workinnorway.no/en/Home
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is connected to the PhD program at the Faculty of Economics and Management, and the faculty will be your employer. Appointment to a PhD position requires that you are admitted to the PhD programme in Industrial Economics and Technology Management within three months of employment, and that you participate in an organized PhD programme during the employment period.

Trondheim is the workplace. For necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.Any statutory leave will be added to the employment period.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important to stay updated on professional and organizational changes and adapt to these.

 
About the application
Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information we have at the application deadline. Therefore, ensure that your application clearly demonstrates how your skills and experiences meet the criteria described above.

The application must contain the following: 

• Motivation letter – The motivation letter must clearly state how the candidate meets the qualification requirements.
• Research plan (maximum one page) – Applicants should provide a brief research plan describing how they would approach one or more of the research questions outlined in the description of the position. The plan should reflect the applicant’s research interests and provide an outline of how they envision contributing to the project objectives.
• CV, diplomas, and certificates 
• Scientific works, including the master thesis. 
• Names and contact information of at least two potential references
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both bachelor's and master's education, in addition to other higher education. Description of the documentation required can be found here. Please note that diploma Supplement is required to attach for European Master Diplomas outside Norway. Chinese applicants are required to provide confirmation of Master Diploma from China Credentials Verification (CHSI).  

If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.  

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential for research will also count in the assessment of the candidates.  

NTNU is committed to following the evaluation criteria for research quality according to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and the commitments in CoARA (responsible research assessment and recognition of a broader range of academic contributions in line with NTNU's societal mission).

Incomplete applications will not be considered.
General information
A public applicant list with names, ages, job titles, and municipalities of residence will be prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to reserve yourself from being included on the public applicant list, this must be justified. The assessment will be made in accordance with applicable laws. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is Norway's technology capital with a population of over 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens, and general equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized childcare is readily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers excellent educational opportunities (including international schools) and opportunities to enjoy nature, culture, and family life, with low crime rates and clean air quality.

Questions about the position can be directed to Professor Asgeir Tomasgard (asgeir.tomasgard @ntnu.no) or Professor Anne Neumann (anne.neumann@ntnu.no).

If you have any questions regarding the employment process, please contact HR Advisor Oddny Lyngvær at oddny.lyngvar@ntnu.no.

jobs.occupation: Postdoktor i idrettsvitenskap
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder, Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap er det ledig en 100% stilling som postdoktor i idrettsvitenskap, tilknyttet Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, for en periode på tre, eventuelt fire år. Arbeidssted er for tiden Campus Kristiansand. Tiltredelse etter avtale med fakultetet.

Fakultetet har fem institutter: Institutt for ernæring og folkehelse, Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap, Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, Institutt for psykologi og Institutt for psykososial helse. Postdoktorstillingen vil være tilknyttet forskningsgruppen PAHLS (Physical Activity and Health across the LifeSpan). I tillegg har instituttet forskningsgruppene SPADE (Sport Performance and Development Environments) og ROPE (Research in Outdoor Education and Physical Education).
Arbeidsoppgaver
I samarbeid med nasjonale og internasjonale forskningsinstitusjoner, kreftforeningen, rehabiliteringsinstitusjon og flere kommuner på Agder, og basert på erfaringer gjort i LETSGO-forskningsprosjekt (Lifestyle and Empowerment Techniques in Survivorship of Gynecologic Oncology - Universitetet i Agder), skal det utvikles en digital smarttelefonapplikasjon (app) med tilhørende opplæringsmodul. Denne skal utvikles sammen med brukere (individer berørt av kreft, helsearbeidere) og inneholde ulike fysisk aktivitets- og treningskomponenter. Videre skal denne implementeres i flere frisklivssentraler i kommuner på Agder. Vi skal evaluere implementeringen av denne. Deretter skal det lages en plan for hvordan app og opplæringsmodul kan rulles ut til alle landets kommuner. 

Den som ansettes vil sammen med prosjektleder ha ansvar for å utvikle studieprotokoll, kvalitetssikring av datainnsamling, harmonisering av data og koordinering av prosjektsamarbeidet mellom de involverte aktører involvert i prosjekter. Vedkommende skal også ha et spesielt ansvar for utviklingen av applikasjonen (sammen med andre forskere ved UiA samt UiAs IT-avdeling) samt implementeringsdelen i prosjektet. I tillegg skal det skrives forskningsartikler på allerede innsamlede og kommende data innenfor fagfeltet fysisk aktivitet/trening ved kreftsykdom. Det forventes at den aktuelle postdoktoren skal drive selvstendig forskning innen rammene for det nevnte prosjektet. Dersom det er aktuelt med undervisning/veiledning legges det også til rette for at kandidaten kan følge kurs i universitetspedagogikk (UniPed). Det er også ønskelig at kandidaten følger karriereutviklingsprogram alla postdoktorprogram. Den som tilsettes i stillingen vil få én faglig veileder.
Nødvendige kvalifikasjoner
Doktorgrad i idrettsvitenskap eller fagområde med relevans for utlysningen. Aktuelle søkere må ha fått godkjent avhandlingen innen søknadsfristen

Arbeidsspråket ved Universitetet i Agder er norsk. Den som ansettes må beherske norsk eller et annet skandinavisk språk, skriftlig og muntlig. Det kreves gode kunnskaper i engelsk, skriftlig og muntlig. 

Ansettelsesvilkår for stilling som postdoktor fremgår av Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.
Ønskede kvalifikasjoner
• Erfaring fra prosjektledelse eller koordinering av prosjekter
• Erfaring med bruk av bevegelsesmålere-/sensorer (aktivitetsmålere, pulsklokker m.m.) i prosjekter
• God teknologisk innsikt; blant annet bruk av smarttelefonapplikasjoner i forskning
• Erfaring med forskning innenfor fagfeltet trening/fysisk aktivitet ved kreftsykdom
• Kjennskap til implementeringsdesign og -metoder
• Erfaring med kvantitative forskningsmetoder, spesialt longitudinelle design
• Det er ønskelig at søkerne har disputert i løpet av de siste fem årPersonlige egenskaper
• Selvstendig
• Gode samarbeidsegenskaper
• Faglig engasjement
• Evne til å sette seg inn i nye problemstillinger og metodetilnærminger
Personlige egenskaper og egnethet for stillingen vil bli vektlagt.
Vi tilbyr
• Faglig utvikling i en stor, spennende og samfunnsviktig organisasjon
• Et godt, inkluderende og mangfoldig arbeidsmiljø
• Moderne lokaliteter og et allsidig velferdstilbud
• Medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse
Mer om UiA som arbeidsplass.

Stillingen lønnes etter Statens lønnsregulativ lønnsplan 17.510, kode 1352 postdoktor, kr. 690 000 – 750 000 brutto pr år. For spesielt godt kvalifiserte søkere kan høyere lønn vurderes. Fra lønnen går det lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse. 
Generell informasjon
UiA er et åpent og inkluderende universitet. Vi har tro på at mangfold beriker arbeidsplassen og gjør oss bedre. Vi oppfordrer derfor kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke uavhengig av kjønn, alder, kulturell bakgrunn, nedsatt funksjonsevne eller “hull i CV-en". 

Kvinner oppfordres spesielt til å søke stillingen. 

Den som ansettes, har rettigheter og plikter etter de retningslinjer som til enhver tid gjelder for stillingen. Ansettelse foretas av Ansettelsesutvalget for undervisnings- og forskerstillinger ved Universitetet i Agder. 

Aktuelle kandidater vil bli innkalt til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser etter nærmere avtale med søkeren. Det kan bli foretatt bakgrunnssjekk for å verifisere opplysninger som kommer frem av tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med søkerens samtykke, og ansettelse i stillingen forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette. Mer om ansettelsesprosessen.  

I henhold til offentlighetsloven § 25, 2.ledd kan søker be om ikke å bli oppført på den offentlige søkerlista. Universitetet kan likevel beslutte at navnet på søkeren skal offentliggjøres. Søker vil bli varslet i forkant ved eventuell offentliggjøring. 
Søknad

jobs.occupation: UX Designer in Growth team
jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale up which has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionize livestock management we need more top-notch competence in our Product team, and we are now looking for a Growth Designer. Elevate your career with us and be at the forefront of innovation in agricultural technology!

We're looking for a Growth Designer to own the user experience of how farmers discover, buy and grow with Nofence. You'll design the website, purchase journey and growth products like our referral and partner programs, and use experiments and data to decide what ships next. You'll be part of the Growth team's leadership trio alongside the VP Growth and Tech Lead, setting the UX bar and helping shape what we build.
About the roleThe main responsibilities for this role will be:
• 
Design the purchase journey: Own the UX of the first-time buyer funnel and checkout, so smaller farms can buy on their own and larger farms move smoothly into a conversation with sales.

• 
Shape the website: Own information architecture, page design and improve conversion across markets, working closely with our Growth Manager

• 
Build growth products: Design our referral and partner programs end to end, across app, web and email.

• 
Cross-Functional collaboration: Work with other teams to align patterns, coordinate releases, and remove seams between journeys. Share insights, resolve dependencies, and contribute to a consistent experience across the app.

• 
Interaction design: Create engaging, intuitive interfaces and flows. Move from low-fidelity sketches to high-fidelity prototypes and ready-to-build specifications.

• 
Collaborative problem solving: Work closely with UX designers, and the broader Growth team to tackle complex design challenges and deliver feasible solutions that meet user needs.

• 
User-centered design: Plan and run discovery, concept tests, and usability evaluations. Use findings to inform prioritisation, iteration, and acceptance criteria.

• 
Stakeholder engagement: Communicate decisions, trade-offs, and user insights with clarity. Ensure shared understanding and buy-in for your domain's direction. 
About youThe right candidate is preferred to have the following qualifications:
• 
Portfolio is needed to showcase your work

• 
You have 5+ years of experience as a product, UX or growth designer, ideally with e-commerce, subscription or self-serve purchase flows with a track record of successfully delivered projects

• 
Proficiency in AI, design and prototyping tools such as Figma is a must and you have strong interaction and UI skills and move easily from rough sketches to build-ready designs.

• 
Fluent English oral and written communication skills. Our working language is English.

• 
Relevant degree/diploma/certificate in Design, HCI, or equivalent.

We are looking for someone who is:
• 
You make design decisions with data and are comfortable with funnels, conversion metrics and experiment results.

• 
You're commercially curious and understand how design affects conversion and acquisition cost.

• 
You work independently and own outcomes, not just deliverables.

• 
You're comfortable shipping a good first version and improving it over time.

• 
Exceptional design skills with a deep understanding of user-centred design principles and methodologies.

• 
You communicate clearly and can explain design trade-offs to developers, marketers and leadership alike.

• 
Excellent facilitation skills, with the ability to partake in workshops and design sprints that drive collaboration and innovation.

• 
Comfortable with working cross-functionally collaborating with different stakeholders to find solutions and drive decisions to impact design.

• 
You speak up early when a plan or deadline doesn't look realistic, and you share decisions openly with the team.

• 
You're friendly, curious and thrive in a fast-moving team where priorities shift.
About Us
As a company still scaling up, our way of working is continuously evolving, and you will have the opportunity to make an impact on how we do things. We are passionate about product development, animal welfare, farmer welfare and sustainable agriculture. We genuinely believe our grazing technology is the biggest technological change in agriculture since the tractor!

So far, our clients have used Nofence in a range of creative ways, including regenerative cattle farming, conservation grazing with goats, regenerative grazing with sheep, and even government work! Yet we have only just scratched the surface, and already have 250 million hours of operation on animals with recorded behaviour data to explore.

Still curious? Visit our website.

The Product team is currently a team of 15 employees working with Product development, UX Design and Global Customer Support. We're excited to add a Growth Designer to our team who's not only skilled in interaction design but also embodies the collaborative and friendly spirit of Nofence. We believe in cooperation, adaptiveness, and a fun and relaxed working environment!
What we bring to the table
At Nofence, we are not your typical 9-to-5 gig. We are a dynamic scale-up, creating a work atmosphere that's anything but ordinary. It's a place where dedication and innovation are the norm, offering great opportunities for your personal and professional growth.

If you're the right fit, you will be part of a tight-knit team, supporting each other to make a real impact on the agricultural industry. With offices in Oslo for the city strollers and our Molde office surrounded by nature for the outdoor enthusiasts, we've got the best of both worlds.

We believe in seeing results fast. As a Growth Designer in our team, your work won't be lost in the bureaucratic shuffle. You'll witness the immediate impact of your contributions in real-time, influencing the evolution of our cutting-edge virtual fencing solution for livestock.

Join us, where ambition meets reality, and let's keep pushing the boundaries in the world of agri-tech!We will evaluate candidates continuously.

Are you ready to change pasture? Just like the soil needs a balanced diversity of nutrients to thrive, a company needs a diversity of hearts and minds. jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale-up that has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionise livestock management, we will need top-notch competence in our Engineering team, and we are now looking for an Electronics Engineer.

The product is small, solar-assisted and combines GNSS, LTE, Bluetooth, and many other technologies, so every design decision is a system integration problem. Join the NPD team that takes it from concept to pilot production.

What you’ll do

• 
Design schematics and PCB layouts, and review designs with the team

• 
Bring up new boards, subcircuits and reusable modules

• 
Test and validate hardware from first prototype to pilot production

• 
Build lab setups and find root causes when things break

• 
Work with the embedded team on low power consumption. On a solar-powered device, every microamp counts

What we’re looking for

• 
Bachelor’s or Master’s in Electrical Engineering or similar

• 
Boards you have taken from schematic to working hardware, and a story about what went wrong on the way

• 
Strong fundamentals: analogue, power and digital design, signal integrity, EMC basics, power optimisation

• 
Confidence with oscilloscope, spectrum analyser, DMM and PCBA debugging and testing

• 
Experience with a professional PCB CAD tool. We’re moving from Altium to KiCad.

• 
Fluent English

Nice to have

• 
RF and antenna design

• 
Experience with integrating GNSS, LTE or Bluetooth in a single device

• 
Complex electromechanical products in harsh environments

• 
CE, FCC and ISED certification

• 
Python for test scripting

What we offer

• 
Short path from idea to impact: you’ll see your work in the field

• 
Visits to customers and their animals, to see how the product lives in reality

• 
Room to grow towards senior or specialist roles

• 
Location: Trondheim or Molde

About the Application

We will evaluate candidates continuously. If you have any questions about Nofence or regarding the application, please reach out to our Engineering Manager, Kjetil Grimsæth.

About Nofence

Managing livestock has always been a challenge. Humanity has tried everything from herding with dogs to walling the animals in with barbed wire, electric, and wooden fences, but these are costly and time-consuming solutions and often in conflict with the local wildlife. It has also left vast areas of potential pasture overgrown and underutilized.

Until now.

Enter virtual fences. What started as a small group of farmers and engineers with a big idea has become Nofence – the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock.

What we bring to the table

At Nofence, we're not your typical 9-to-5 gig. We're a dynamic scale-up, creating a work atmosphere that's anything but ordinary. It's a place where dedication and innovation are the norm, offering great opportunities for your personal and professional growth.

We believe in seeing results fast. As an engineer with us, your work won't be lost in the bureaucratic shuffle. You'll witness the immediate impact of your contributions in real-time, influencing the evolution of our cutting-edge virtual fencing solution for livestock.

Join us, where ambition meets reality, and let's keep pushing the boundaries in the world of agri-tech!

At reTyre, you’re not just joining a company — you’re joining a groundbreaking industrial journey together with a great team of innovators.

We’ve built the world’s first sustainable tire factory, right in the heart of Ski, 20 min outside of Oslo.

We are now looking for a skilled and hands-on Process Engineer with Management skills to join the Manufacturing team and drive our mission forward. Our team is internationally diverse, young, energetic, and united by a passion for innovation, sustainability, and growth. Every day, we challenge the conventional and push the boundaries of what manufacturing can be — for the benefit of people and the planet.

The role

The Process Engineer will work daily on the shop floor to test and improve processes, troubleshoot issues, and create accurate documentation and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Continuously improve process efficiency and stability.

You are experienced in a Manufacturing/Production and feel confident entering this role with your existing skillsets and are still hungry for further growth and development.

You find it motivating to be a part of a Company's journey going from startup to scaleup, that offers a different kind of environment than other typical traditional manufacturing companies offer.

Experience matters — but so does attitude and passion.

Qualifications

Technical diploma or degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.

• 
Strong hands-on experience with production machinery and process optimization.

• 
Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

• 
Ability to work independently and in a team-oriented environment.

•

Proactive and adaptable in a start-up environment.

Strong English communication skills, both written and spoken.

Proactive and solution-oriented.

• 
Motivated by innovation and fast-changing environments.

Flexible and comfortable working in a modern, small-team environment with real influence.

Precise, organized, structured and good work ethics.

• 
Good communication skills.

• 
Independent and self-driven.

• 
A positive team player who contributes to a great work culture.
